Doctoral student in Automatic Control with focus on Datacenter Control

Lund University, The Faculty of Engineering, Department

Description of the workplace

Automatic Control is an exciting and broad subject, covering both advanced mathematics and hands-on engineering. Historically, it has been instrumental in many areas, from the early development of telecommunications to the space race. Today, driven by the need to engineer ever larger systems, Automatic Control is more relevant than ever.

The department of Automatic control has a stimulating and international environment with PhD students, postdocs, and teachers coming from all corners of the world. Research and teaching are conducted in an open and progressive atmosphere with collaborations both within academia and with industry, nationally as well as internationally. A PhD degree from the Department of Automatic control gives you the perfect base for an exciting career, be it in academia or industry.

Lund University and the Department of Automatic Control welcome applicants with diverse backgrounds and experiences. We regard equality and diversity as a strength and an asset. For more information on being a doctoral student at the department, please have a look at our research videos: Research | Department of Automatic Control (lth.se).

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se. https://www.lth.se/english/study-at-lth/phd-studies/

AEGIS — Adaptive Grid-Interactive Edge Datacenter Fleets is a European Marie Skłodowska-Curie Action (MSCA) research and training network. It is funded by the EU and trains 15 PhD students from 2026 to 2030. The main host for this position is Department of Automatic Control at Lund University. As part of the program you will spend two 3-months visits with partners in the network: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (Switzerland) and Elisa (Finland). Marie Skłodowska-Curie fellowships are among the most respected PhD positions in Europe. The position is only open to applicants that have not lived, studied, or worked in Sweden for more than 12 months in the 36 months before applying.

More information about the project is available at the website https://aegis-dn.eu

Subject and project description

The AEGIS project sits where two fast-growing fields meet: datacentres and AI infrastructure on one side, energy and power systems on the other. Few people today can work across both, so the skills you build here are scarce and in high demand. Specifically there is a gap between a high-level goal like “cut carbon now” and the low-level controls of a site’s cooling, batteries, and compute hardware. In this project you close that gap.

You will build a control layer that takes “intents” and translates them into a coordinated set of actions across the site’s physical assets. The models close the loop and tune themselves online using both classical control, AI, and reinforcement learning.

In the project you will work on:

Designing an intent language that captures carbon, flexibility, and cost. Breaking high-level intents down into control actions. Tuning power-performance and thermal models online.

What you will deliver:

Control software that turns intents into commands, with measured latency. Practical control systems using real-world data from experiments. A telemetry system that reports headroom and runs without breaking service-level limits in test scenarios.

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme, which includes participation in research projects as well as third cycle courses, seminars and conferences.

The PhD position consists of three main aspects, and the work duties include:

  • research project, including authoring papers and traveling to conferences, seminars etc.
  • postgraduate courses, given locally, nationally and internationally (90 ECTS credits)
  • teaching (no more than 20%), including lab supervision and exam responsibilities. This part may also include departmental services, such as working with equality and diversity, arranging events etc

Qualifications

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantial equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in Automatic Control if the applicant has:

  • knowledge corresponding to course FRTF05 (previously FRT010) Automatic Control, Basic Course and a second cycle specialisation of relevance to the subject, and
  • an MSc in engineering or corresponding qualification

The standard MSCA eligibility criteria also apply:

No doctoral degree. At the date of recruitment you must not yet hold a PhD. Mobility rule. You must not have lived or done your main activity (work or studies) in Sweden for more than 12 months in the 36 months just before you are recruited. Short stays such as holidays do not count.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • Very good oral and written proficiency in English.
  • Good language-analytical ability.
  • Curiosity about research and teaching in general, and motivation for the particular research project.
  • Creativity with good ability for cooperation and networking.
  • Good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems.
  • Good written and oral communication skills.
  • Strong mathematical knowledge as demonstrated through university transcripts.

Other qualifications (advantages)

For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as other qualifications:

Strong foundations in

  • Machine learning and reinformement learning.
  • Cloud computing and cloud technology.
  • Low-level programming and Linux kernel experience.

are meriting.

Consideration will be given to good collaborative skills, drive and independence, and how the applicant,through experience and skills, is deemed to have the abilities necessary for successfully completing the third cycle programme.

We offer

Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme.

More about working at Lund University on lu.se. https://www.lunduniversity.lu.se/about-university/work-lund-university

About the employment

The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, starting as soon as possible or March 1, 2027, at the latest. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§.

More about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staffpages. https://www.staff.lu.se/research-and-education/research-support/doctoral-education/terms-employment-doctoral-students

Other

We intend to offer employment to 1 PhD student. A doctoral student will receive a competitive monthly salary of 35 900 SEK with yearly raise.

Those applicants who will be called for interview, might be asked to perform a small test to demonstrate basic competence.

How to apply

Applications shall be written in English and include:

  • CV and a cover letter stating the reasons why you are interested in the doctoral programme/employment and in what way the research project corresponds to your interests and educational background.
  • Copies of issued study certificates and/or awarded degree certificates. These must confirm that you meet the general and specific admission requirements for the doctoral programme and show that you have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral programme project.
  • Other documents you wish to be considered (grade transcripts, contact information for your references, letters of recommendation, etc.)

We welcome your application.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in non-Newtonian fluid mechanics and AI
jobs.department: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences
jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Engineering Mechanics

Within EU doctoral network FairCFD, this project will combine high-performance computing, experiments and artificial intelligence in non-Newtonian flows, with the aim of improving rheological characterisation and modelling. In particular, we will design a digital twin rheometer to reliably measure complex fluid parameters in time-varying and chaotic flows.

We will use modern AI techniques to exploit spatial patterns in the computational and experimental data and optimize parameter sensitivity. The researcher will join the dynamic Complex Fluids Research group, have access to the supercomputing facilities at KTH, the Swedish e-Science Research Centre (SeRC) and the excellent research environment FLOW.

Supervision: Outi Tammisola and Fredrik Lundell are proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission.

Admission requirements

  • Mobility rules - Candidates must not have resided or conducted their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Sweden for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately preceding the recruitment date,

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Game-Theoretic Methods for Multi-Agent Autonomous Systems
jobs.department: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Electrical Engineering

Autonomous systems are increasingly deployed alongside humans to carry out complex coordinated tasks. In these settings, autonomous systems must handle strict spatial and temporal constraints while adapting in real time to supervisory commands, unexpected obstacles, and environmental disturbances. Enabling trustworthy human–robot collaboration calls for new mathematical foundations and computational tools that unify decision-making, planning, and control.

We are seeking an exceptional doctoral student to conduct research at the intersection of game theory and control for multi-agent autonomous systems. The position is part of the Digital Futures project Human-in-the-Loop Autonomy via Hybrid Games. The work will span both mathematical foundations of hybrid games and the design of computationally tractable controllers for deployment on real robotic platforms.

The research will address:

  • Hybrid dynamic games under temporal logic task specifications;
  • Game-theoretic modelling of human–robot interaction;
  • Experimental validation on multi-robot and underwater robotic platforms;

Supervision: Assistant Prof. Giuseppe Belgioioso and Prof. Dimos Dimarogonas are proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission

KTH is now inviting talented and highly motivated candidates to apply for this doctoral position.  The doctoral student will develop new algorithms and well-founded methods, formalize their theoretical foundations, and evaluate them experimentally. The research will be broadly situated in machine learning, including (but not limited to) algorithmic knowledge discovery, graph mining and social network analysis, optimization for machine learning, representation learning, and fair, accountable, and transparent machine learning.

This PhD position in machine learning, will lead to a joint doctoral degree from KTH Royal Institute of Technology (Sweden) and Nanyang Technological University (NTU, Singapore). Project description

Third-cycle subject: Computer Science

The PhD student will work within GEOMANIP, an ERC Starting Grant project that aims to revolutionize the robotic manipulation of deformable objects by uncovering and exploiting their fundamental geometric nature. GEOMANIP proposes a paradigm shift that integrates the differential geometric structure of deformable objects into novel continuum physics-inspired neural representations, serving as the bedrock of a physically-grounded manipulation pipeline encompassing perception, planning, and control. The PhD student will contribute to one or more of the following topics: theoretical foundations and geometric formalization, representation learning, robust perception and geometric state estimation,  robot policy learning and control.

jobs.department: School of Engineering Sciences at KTH
jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Physics, specialization in Nuclear Engineering

The group of Nuclear Power Safety in Division of Nuclear Science and Engineering (NSE) conducts research on accident phenomena of risk importance to existing and future nuclear reactors, and performs safety analysis for nuclear power plants, including design basis accident analysis and severe accident analysis. The research projects involve extensive international cooperation.

We are looking for a doctoral student to carry out frontier research on accident management (AM) during severe accidents of light water reactors. The doctoral student project is supported by the funds from Strålsäkerhetsmyndigheten (SSM).

The successful candidate is expected to (i) digitalize the paper-based, lookup-table-like procedures in the severe accident management guidelines (SAMG) to be chosen, facilitating the realization of the SAMG in case of severe accidents; (ii) develop an AI-aided tool for diagnosis of plant damage state using measured and estimated data (e.g. the simulation results of U.S. NRC codes); and (iii) combine the digitalized SAMG with the AI-aided tool for effective accident management.

Project description

Third-cycle subject: Engineering Mechanics

FLOW is a strong community of researchers engaged in fundamental and applied research in fluid mechanics within the department of Engineering Mechanics.

We are currently seeking an experimental PhD student in fluid mechanics to join the Fluids and Surfaces Group within FLOW. This position offers an exciting opportunity for a highly motivated candidate to contribute to a cutting-edge research program funded by the Swedish Research Council (VR).

The project aims to uncover how complex films, including biological and living films, interact with surrounding fluid flows. Such films are ubiquitous in nature and technological applications, ranging from mucus in the lungs to biofilms on medical devices and ship hulls. When exposed to shear and potentially unsteady flows, these films can deform into complex shapes, exhibit unusual material properties, and evolve over time, thereby creating a dynamic and continuously changing boundary for the flow. At the same time, the films modify the overlying flow, potentially altering frictional resistance as well as the transport and exchange of species.

Despite their importance, the coupled interaction between complex films and fluid flows remains poorly understood. This limits our ability to predict and control these systems and poses major challenges across medical, industrial, and geophysical applications.

In this project, the PhD student will work with and further develop a unique experimental platform for studying complex films under controlled, yet complex, flow conditions. The experimental work will be complemented by continuum modeling of complex materials, data-driven methods, and computational fluid dynamics.

Supervision: Shervin Bagheri is proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission

Project description

Third-cycle subject: Information and Communication Technology

Currently, there are no effective methods for protecting implementations of cryptographic algorithms from fault attacks, where an adversary deliberately injects faults into cryptographic computations to extract sensitive information. This project aims to address this important open problem, with a particular focus on remote attacks. We intend to take into account the impact of fault attacks on cryptographic implementation security from both an offensive perspective (by devising new types of attacks) and a defensive perspective (by designing countermeasures). The overarching challenge is to create defense mechanisms that can withstand fault attacks as the adversary's capabilities grow. By considering mathematical and electrical engineering problems together, the project is expected to create cryptographic implementations in which resistance to fault attacks is incorporated at the design stage rather than addressed later, after a vulnerability is discovered.

The successful candidate is expected to investigate the use of advanced machine learning techniques to enhance both the analysis and mitigation of fault attacks. The insights gained will be used to develop new vulnerability assessment methods and design countermeasures against fault attacks, along with supporting tools.

The work will be carried out in the Hardware Security group at KTH which currently includes five PhD students.

jobs.title: PhD student in Recycling of Solid Electrolytes for All-Solid-State Batteries
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Disciplinary Domain of Science and Technology, Faculty of Chemistry, Department of Chemistry - Ångström Laboratory
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Chemistry - Ångström conducts research and education in the chemistry field. The department has more than 270 employees and has a turnover of 300 million SEK. At the department's six programs, we conduct very successful research of a high international standard. We have a large number of externally funded research projects, often with international cooperation and we see continued good growth in our subject area. The department has education assignments in engineering programs and master's programs. More information is available on our website. Department of Chemistry Ångström Laboratory

The Department of Chemistry – Ångström Laboratory has for many years hosted an environment focused on research and development of materials and their applications within the energy storage area: the Ångström Advanced Battery Centre. We develop novel electrode and electrolyte materials, characterize them, evaluate and improve them with respect to battery performance, and study fundamental chemical processes and properties using both experimental and computational techniques. The research is, as such, both fundamental and applied

Duties 
The project  aims to establish a scientific basis for the recycling of solid electrolytes used in all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs). The project is a collaboration between Uppsala University, KTH Royal Institute of Technology and Université de Lorraine in France, combining expertise in solid-state chemistry, battery materials, hydrometallurgy, purification and crystallization.The project focuses on lithium halide solid electrolytes, an emerging class of materials with high ionic conductivity and promising electrochemical stability. The central goal is to understand how the recycling process and impurities introduced during battery operation and recycling influence the structure, ionic transport and electrochemical performance of resynthesized solid electrolytes. The results will be used to establish precursor quality specifications for closed-loop recycling of solid-state battery materials.

The doctoral student will be based at Uppsala University and will work across the different stages of the recycling process. Key duties include synthesis and structural characterization of lithium-containing halide solid electrolytes, preparation and characterization of solid-state battery cells, ionic transport measurements using impedance spectroscopy, and investigation of the influence of impurities on material and cell performance.

The candidate will also participate in the development and evaluation of recycled precursor materials produced through hydrometallurgical processing. A research stay at Université de Lorraine in France, where the candidate will work on leaching and purification processes, is an integral part of the project. The candidate will also collaborate with researchers at KTH on crystallization and synthesis of purified precursor materials.

The work will involve a combination of synthesis, structural and chemical characterization, electrochemical measurements, data analysis and interpretation. Particular emphasis will be placed on establishing quantitative relationships between precursor composition, impurity content, crystal structure, ionic transport and battery performance.

The duties may also include:

  • Planning and performing air- and moisture-sensitive synthesis of inorganic solid electrolytes
  • Structural and chemical characterization using techniques such as powder X-ray diffraction, SEM-EDS and XPS
  • Ionic transport characterization using temperature-dependent impedance spectroscopy
  • Assembly and electrochemical testing of solid-state battery cells
  • Analysis and interpretation of experimental data
  • Research visits to collaborating institutions in Sweden and France
  • Supervision of degree projects
  • Data analysis and dissemination of research results through scientific publications and conference presentations
  • Teaching at first and second cycle level
  • Administration linked to the tasks above

Requirements 
To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must

  • been awarded a second-cycle degree in Chemistry, Physics, Materials Science, or equivalent/another relevant field, or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • acquired essentially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

The candidate must have:

  • very good oral and written proficiency in English.
  • good organizational and time-management skills.
  • good collaborative skills and the ability to work independently.
  • a strong interest in materials chemistry, solid-state chemistry, energy storage or related fields.
  • experience with experimental laboratory work in chemistry, materials science or a related field.
  • experience with data analysis and scientific writing..

Experience in hydrometallurgy, leaching, solvent extraction or crystallization is considered advantageous but is not required. The project provides the opportunity to develop expertise in these areas through collaboration with KTH and Université de Lorraine.

Consideration will also be given to good collaborative skills, drive and independence, and how the applicant’s experience and skills complement and strengthen ongoing research within the department, and how they stand to contribute to its future development of research on solid-state batteries and circular battery materials.

Additional qualifications 

Experience with battery assembly and electrochemical testing, inorganic synthesis, powder diffraction, or solid-state ionic transport is desirable. Previous experience with air- and moisture-sensitive materials is particularly relevant to the project.

About the employment
The employment is a temporary position according to the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5 § 7. Scope of employment 100 %. Starting date as agreed. Placement: Uppsala

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines.

jobs.title: PhD student in Geophysics
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Earth Sciences
jobs.description_html:
PhD student in Geophysics: Enhancing exploration drilling efficiency through integrated analyses rock formation and drilling data

Are you interested in working with sustainable and responsible exploration drilling of critical raw materials, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at Uppsala University.

The Department of Earth Sciences is Sweden's most comprehensive academic environment for research and education in geoscience. It offers a broad range of expertise that can contribute to solving important societal issues.

Earth is a dynamic and constantly changing planet. To understand how this planet works, our researchers seek answers in the field, through laboratory experiments and advanced models. Our research and education cover a wide range of disciplines, including rocks and minerals, weather and climate, the evolution of life, natural disasters, wind power and energy, environmental and water engineering, and sustainable development.

Our research combines natural sciences and technology with social sciences and is often interdisciplinary. More than 300 people from over 30 countries work at the department, both in Uppsala and at Campus Gotland.

Our six research divisions:

  • Geophysics • Air, Water and Landscape Science • Mineralogy, Petrology and Tectonics
  • Natural Resources and Sustainable Development • Palaeobiology • Wind Energy

For more information see: www.uu.se/earthsciences

Geophysics is about "looking into" and understanding the Earth’s structure, its history and processes-based on measurements of the Earth’s physical properties. In geophysics we use quantitative physical methods to investigate the Earth and its environment. In addition, physical property measurements, rock mechanical field testing, scientific drilling and numerical modelling are employed to investigate the subsurface structures and processes. The Geophysics program currently runs several national and international projects and has a wealth of world-class infrastructures. It also leads the Smart Exploration Research Center (SERC) (www.smartexploration.se). SERC is funded by the Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research, with members from four Swedish universities, three mining companies, four technology companies, and one development company. The PhD project will be conducted in close collaboration with Epiroc, Nordic Iron and Lund University.

In this PhD project, you will be enrolled as a PhD student at Uppsala University in close collaboration with Epiroc Rock Drills AB in Örebro. You will mainly be placed at Uppsala University, Uppsala. During shorter periods, you will also be placed at Epiroc Rock Drills AB in Örebro and participate if field work.

Access to certain technology or data associated with industry partners within the project may be subject to applicable export control legislation and will be managed in accordance with current regulations.

Duties

The PhD candidate will conduct research within SERC, focusing on sustainable and responsible exploration of critical raw materials. The overarching aim of the PhD project is to develop a framework for integrating rock formation and drilling data to improve exploration drilling efficiency, thereby contribute to more sustainable and responsible exploration drilling.

The project combines geoscience and drilling technology, with a focus on diamond core drilling in crystalline rock. The PhD candidate will develop advanced theoretical, technical and practical expertise in the technical and operational challenges of the drilling process, as well as geoscientific methods for subsurface characterization.

The work involves data acquisition in connection with exploration drilling, borehole logging, in-situ testing, drill core analyses, and laboratory testing. Separate and integrated analyses of these datasets will be used to investigate potential relationships between rock formation properties, drilling data, and exploration drilling efficiency. 

The doctoral student  will work in close collaboration with academic and industry research groups contributing to stronger collaboration and knowledge exchange between these communities. The PhD candidate is expected to combine theoretical and practical work, work both independently and collaboratively, spend parts of the project period with industry partners, and participate in field and laboratory work.

Requirements

To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must:

  • hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in geophysics, geology, rock mechanics, drilling technology, physics, earth sciences or a similar field, or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

We are seeking a candidate with strong interests in exploration drilling in crystalline rocks and methods for subsurface characterisation, both in-situ and in the laboratory. Good oral and written proficiency in English is required.

Additional qualifications

Experience in various types of data acquisition and analysis, such as measurement while drilling (MWD), logging while drilling (LWD), borehole logging, rock stress measurements, drill core logging, and rock mechanic laboratory testing, is considered a merit. Experience in integrating and analysing different types of drilling data, rock formation data, or a combination of these is also considered a merit. The ability to work both independently and collaboratively is considered a merit. Proficiency in spoken and written Swedish is a merit, because communication in Swedish may be required during fieldwork and collaboration with industry partners. A driving license is a merit, as it may be required for fieldwork.

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines. A PhD position is full-time for four years. Teaching or administrative duties at the department corresponding to a maximum of 20 per cent may occur by agreement. The employment is extended to a corresponding extent.

Application

  1. A personal letter describing yourself, your research interests, why you wish to pursue doctoral studies, and why you are a suitable candidate for this specific position and project (maximum 2 pages).
  2. A curriculum vitae (CV).
  3. A verified transcript of records and a brief description of your educational background.
  4. A copy of your Master's degree certificate (or equivalent advanced-level degree certificate).
  5. Your degree project/thesis report (finished or in draft form).
  6. Names and contact details of two references (including email addresses and telephone numbers).

About the employment

The employment is a temporary position according to the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5 § 7. Scope of employment 100 %. Starting date 15 January 2027, or as agreed. Placement: Uppsala

Vill du arbeta som doktorand i ett projekt som syftar till att stärka en likvärdig och rättssäker bedömning av intellektuell funktionsnedsättning, med stöd av kompetenta och trevliga kollegor i en internationell miljö? Vill du ha en arbetsgivare som satsar på ett hållbart medarbetarskap och erbjuder trygga, förmånliga arbetsvillkor? Välkommen att söka anställning som doktorand i barn- och ungdomspsykiatri på Uppsala universitet.

Institutionen för medicinska vetenskaper är en stor klinisk institution med ca 250 anställda och över 900 personer som är anknutna via Akademiska Sjukhuset. Institutionen har en bred forskningsprofil med starka forskargrupper inom en rad områden. Forskningen äger rum i nära anslutning till den kliniska verksamheten vid Akademiska sjukhuset och omfattar såväl grundläggande studier kring sjukdomsorsaker som utveckling och utvärdering av förbättrad diagnostik och nya behandlingsmetoder. Mer om institutionens verksamhet finns på https://www.uu.se/institution/medicinska-vetenskaper/.

Projektet leds av docent Matilda Frick, verksam i forskargruppen inom barn och ungdomspsykiatri som leds av professor Agnieszka Butwicka. Projektet avser undersöka hur kognitiva nivå, adaptiv förmåga och demografisk sammansättning hos barn med lindrig intellektuell funktionsnedsättning förändrats över tid, hur den diagnostiska processen uppfattas av utredande psykologer och vårdnadshavare samt hur den diagnostiska precisionen kan öka för att säkerställa likvärdiga och rättssäkra bedömningar.

Meriterande är erfarenhet av datainsamling, utredning av intellektuell funktionsnedsättning samt arbetslivserfarenhet inom anpassad skola.

jobs.title: PhD student in Physical Chemistry with focus on perovskite solar cells
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Chemistry - Ångström Laboratory
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Chemistry - Ångström conducts research and education in the chemistry field. The department has more than 270 employees and has a turnover of 300 million SEK. At the department's six programs, we conduct very successful research of a high international standard. We have a large number of externally funded research projects, often with international cooperation and we see continued good growth in our subject area. The department has education assignments in engineering programs and master's programs. More information is available on our website. www.uu.se/en/department/chemistry-angstrom-laboratory?languageld=1

Duties
The research is related to perovskite solar cells (PSCs), a novel photovoltaic technology that has quickly reached efficiencies as high as that of silicon. PSCs are, however, much easier and cheaper to produce. Unfortunately, their stability is still insufficient. Ion conductivity in the material could be the main reason. In this project the PhD student will investigate the ion conductivity in perovskite thin films and solar cells and determine its effect on performance and stability. Furthermore, strategies to control ion conductivity in perovskites will be developed.

The PhD student will prepare perovskite films and solar cells in different configurations using wet-chemical deposition methods. Along with vapor-deposited films and solar cell devices from our collaborator, these will be investigated, using electrochemical techniques and advanced spectroscopies. This project is done within the consortium SOLVE - Solar Electricity Research Centre, Sweden (https://www.uu.se/en/research/solve).

The main duties of doctoral students are to devote themselves to their research studies, which includes participating in research projects and third cycle courses. The work duties can also include teaching and other departmental duties (no more than 20%). The PhD student should design, plan, perform the experimental work, as well as critically analyze and discuss the results, initially with close guidance by the supervisor. As the PhD students develop, they are expected to become more independent in taking the initiative and planning the research. The students are expected to participate actively in workshops and to present their results at scientific conferences as well as in scientific peer-reviewed journals.

jobs.title: PhD student in Limnology: Modelling phytoplankton succession in lakes
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Ecology and Genetics
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in exploring the driving processes behind phytoplankton succession in lakes and assessing how phytoplankton will respond to future environmental changes? Are you looking for an employer, who invests in sustainable career development and offers supportive working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD student position at Uppsala University, which will be placed at the Department of Ecology and Genetics within the Limnology program.

The Limnology program is an internationally renowned working environment with staff and students from all over the world. The program engages in research and education on the biogeochemistry and ecology of inland waters, spanning from microscopic to global scale. The program actively promotes a collegial and inclusive research culture through regular social activities, encouraging well-being, creativity, and professional growth.

Project Description
Phytoplankton form an important foundation of lake food webs and their community composition changes markedly throughout the year in response to physical and chemical changes as well as predation pressures. These changes are in turn moderated by different functional traits between groups, which determine how they respond to environmental conditions. Using models, we can study how environmental changes (such as climate warming, eutrophication, and extreme weather events) influence successional patterns in phytoplankton and identify conditions that create windows of opportunity for specific functional groups. We can then use these models to assess potential future changes. We are seeking a highly-motivated PhD student who is keen to use process-based biogeochemical models to investigate these dynamics. The outcomes of this work will improve our ability to forecast changes in phytoplankton communities, with direct application to lake ecosystem functioning and drinking water provisioning. The position is based at Uppsala University’s Department of Ecology and Genetics, within the Limnology program.

Duties
Your duties will have a strong focus on data handling and process-based, dynamical modelling, but also include teaching, course work, and collaborating in research teams.

Requirements
To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must

  • hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in limnology, aquatic ecology, environmental sciences, geoscience, biology, environmental engineering or other relevant subjects at the time of employment, or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

Candidates who have not yet completed their degree but are expected to meet the degree requirements before the start date are encouraged to apply.

This work lies in the intersection of physics, biogeochemistry, and ecology, and has a strong numerical emphasis. jobs.title: Doktorand i resilienta elkraftsystem
jobs.description_html:
Elektrifiering och digitalisering tillhör framtidens största områden för omställning till hållbara samhällen. Institutionen för elektroteknik bedriver framgångsrik forskning och utbildning inom dessa områden – däribland förnybara energikällor och elfordon, industriell IoT, 6G kommunikation och trådlösa sensornät men även forskning och utbildning inom Life Science, hälsoteknik, smarta elektroniska sensorer och medicinska system. Institutionen för elektroteknik är en internationell miljö med ca 170 medarbetare som bidrar till viktiga tekniska energi- och hälsolösningar vid Ångströmlaboratoriet.

Vi söker nu en Doktorand i resilienta elkraftsystem.

Kom och jobba med oss!
Tjänsten är placerad vid avdelningen för elektricitetslära inom institutionen för elektroteknik. Här hittar du en trevlig arbetsmiljö med ett aktivt doktorandnätverk och en mängd experimentella projekt. Avdelningen samarbetar med svenska företag – både offentliga och privata – samt andra intressenter inom de olika forskningsområdena. Vi ser fram emot din ansökan. Var med och bygg framtiden med oss!

Läs mer om våra förmåner och hur det är att jobba inom Uppsala.

Projektbeskrivning

Elkraftsystemets betydelse för samhällets funktion ställer ökade krav på robusthet, återhämtningsförmåga och effektiv drift, särskilt i ljuset av ett försämrat säkerhetsläge, ökad elektrifiering och ett högre nyttjande av befintliga transmissions- och distributionsnät av el. Inom dessa doktorandprojekt kommer avancerad modellering, systemsimuleringar och scenarioanalyser att användas för att utveckla metoder som stärker elkraftsystemets resiliens vid kris, krig och andra ansträngda driftförhållanden.

Projekten omfattar såväl optimerad drift av elkraftsystemet efter omfattande störningar som utveckling av nya nyckeltal, prognosmetoder och styrstrategier för att mäta, analysera och förbättra elkraftsystemets förmåga att upprätthålla leveransen av el under ansträngda förhållanden. Arbetet sker i nära samverkan med energibranschen och omfattar tillämpningar i simuleringsverktyg. Projekten genomförs inom kompetenscentret RESILIENT, ett nationellt forskningscentrum som samlar akademi, industri och samhällsaktörer för att utveckla framtidens resilienta och hållbara energisystem genom nära samverkan mellan forskning och tillämning.

Arbetsuppgifter

  • Bedriva forskning inom resilienta elkraftsystem med fokus på elsystemets funktion, drift och återgång under kris-, krigs- och andra ansträngda driftförhållanden.
  • Utveckla metoder, modeller och beslutsstöd för att stärka elkraftsystemets robusthet, resiliens och återhämtningsförmåga.
  • Genomföra teoretiska studier i kombination med modellutveckling, systemsimuleringar och scenarioanalyser för att validera forskningsresultat.
  • Använda och vidareutveckla modeller i simuleringsverktyg såsom PowerFactory, PowerWorld och PSS®E eller motsvarande.
  • Analysera frågor kopplade till systemdrift, systemåterhämtning, resiliensmått, prognoser och styrstrategier för framtidens elkraftsystem.
  • Publicera forskningsresultat i vetenskapliga tidskrifter och presentera resultaten vid nationella och internationella konferenser.
  • Samverka med industri, myndigheter och andra forskningsaktörer inom kompetenscentret RESILIENT.

Undervisning och övrig institutionstjänstgöring kan komma att ingå i arbetsuppgifterna, dock max 20% av arbetstiden.

Kvalifikationskrav

Behörig till utbildning på forskarnivå är den som har

  • avlagt examen på avancerad nivå så som civilingenjörsexamen inom energisystem, elektroteknik, system i teknik och samhälle eller motsvarande, eller
  • fullgjort minst 240 högskolepoäng varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå inklusive ett självständigt arbete om minst 15 högskolepoäng, eller
  • på något annat sätt förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.
  • Säkerhetsprövning ska kunna genomföras för att kunna samarbeta med säkerhetsklassade svenska myndigheter.
  • Du behöver vara målmedveten, strukturerad och analytisk samt ha ett öga för problemlösning och tycka om att jobba mot mål.

Vi lägger stor vikt vid personliga egenskaper såsom god samarbets- och kommunikationsförmåga samt förmåga att arbeta självständigt.

Kandidaten ska ha god/ mycket god förmåga att uttrycka sig på engelska och svenska, både i tal och skrift.

Meriterande

  • Kunskap inom statisk och dynamisk analys av elkraftsystem.
  • Helhetsperspektiv och förståelse för system och hur olika system sammanlänkas.

Om anställningen

Tidsbegränsad anställning i 48 månader, enligt HF 5 kap § 7. Omfattningen är heltid. Tillträde 2027-01-01, eller enligt överenskommelse. Placeringsort Uppsala.

Bestämmelser för doktorander återfinns i Högskoleförordningen 5 kap §§ 1-7 samt i universitetets regler och riktlinjer.

Upplysningar om anställningen lämnas av
Professor Robert Eriksson, robert.eriksson@uu.se.

Instruktioner för ansökan
Ansökan ska innehålla 1) ett brev som beskriver dig själv, dina forskningsintressen och varför du vill doktorera, 2) ditt CV, 3) en kort beskrivning av din utbildning, 4) en kopia av din masterexamen och dina kursbetyg samt en kopia av din masteruppsats 5) eventuellt andra handlingar som du önskar åberopa, 6) namn och kontaktuppgifter till referenspersoner (e-postadress och telefonnummer), och 7) eventuella publikationer. Ansökan bör skrivas på svenska.

Välkommen med din ansökan senast den 12 november 2026. UFV-PA 2026/2920.

jobs.title: PhD student position in Bioinformatics/Evolutionary Microbiology
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Medical Biochemistry and Microbiology
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Medical Biochemistry and Microbiology (IMBIM) at Uppsala University provides a broad international environment for research and teaching. Research at IMBIM spans biochemistry, molecular and cell biology, structural biology, tumour biology, comparative genetics, functional genomics, immunology, bacteriology and virology. The research has a basic-science orientation, with strong relevance to mechanisms of health and disease in both animals and humans. More info: Research – Department of Medical Biochemistry and Microbiology – Uppsala University

We are looking for a highly motivated PhD student to join the project “A two-billion-year history of infections: evolution of host-adaptation in early Gammaproteobacteria”, funded by the Swedish Research Council and led by Lionel Guy. The PhD student will be located at the Biomedical Centre, Uppsala, Sweden.

Project description

The ability to feed on other organisms through phagocytosis is a crucial step in the evolution of eukaryotes, a prerequisite for food webs, multicellularity and probably the acquisition of mitochondria. It also paved the way for intracellular parasitism, as some bacteria avoided digestion by their hosts and multiplied in the nutrient-rich cytoplasm.

Here, we focus on the Deep-branching Intracellular Gammaproteobacteria (DIG), a large group of related bacteria (e.g. Legionella and Francisella) with a wide variety of host-adaptation strategies. We hypothesize that the last common ancestor of DIG appeared during eukaryogenesis, 2 billion years ago, and was among the first bacteria to infect eukaryotes.

In this project, the PhD student will gather a solid set of DIG genomes, including isolates belonging to 30 novel species of Legionella, reconstruct their evolutionary history, assess their metabolic potential, and identify their host-adaptation genes. They will screen genomes for horizontal gene transfers from early eukaryotes or Asgard archaea and specifically analyse the evolution of the Legionella genus.

A better understanding of the relationships between the first eukaryotes and their early invaders will shed light on eukaryogenesis, and particularly on the role of phagocytosis.

Required Qualifications

To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must

  • hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in bioinformatics, molecular biology, microbiology, microbial ecology or a similar field or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

The degree should be completed, or expected to be completed, before March 2027.

  • Documented coding skills in Python or R
  • Experience in using and/or developing methods in metagenomics and molecular evolution
  • Background understanding of, and interest in, microbial evolution
  • Proficiency in spoken and written English
  • Ability to plan, carry out and complete research projects independently
  • Creativity and good teamwork skills

 Desirable qualifications

  • Experience of building pipelines for high-performance computing (HPC) clusters
  • Competence in handling large datasets
  • Experience with DNA extraction and sequencing library preparation 

The selection is based on the following criteria: completion of the above qualifications, grades in relevant courses, the relevance of those courses to the research programme, and previous experience of work and research in the wider area of the project described above. An overall assessment of the applicant will be made in order to employ the best possible candidate, who can succeed in the doctoral studies and contribute to a positive development of the research programme. Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities, including analytical ability, accuracy, flexibility and collaborative skills.

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines.

The employment is a temporary position according to the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5 § 7. Scope of employment 100 %. Starting date as soon as possible or as agreed. Placement: Uppsala

jobs.title: PhD student in Media and Communication Studies
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Informatics and Media
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in working with research in Media and Communication, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a position as PhD student in Media and communication studies at Uppsala University.

The Department of Informatics and Media has a broad research profile grounded in contemporary research fields, including information systems, interaction design, and media and communication. Within the discipline of Media and Communication Studies, research focuses on various forms of communication and media in both global and local contexts. The work within the research environment is connected through a deeply interdisciplinary and critical approach, employing both qualitative and quantitative methods. We study media and communication as fundamental to understanding contemporary social change as well as to defining the conditions and challenges of human coexistence. 

Duties
The position is a fully funded doctoral studentship in Media and Communication Studies at the Department of Informatics and Media. Doctoral education comprises four years of full-time study. The doctoral candidate is expected to devote the main part of their working time to doctoral education (see project description below) and to actively participate in the department’s seminar activities, workshops, conferences, and similar events. Other duties, such as teaching and research administration – in English and/or Swedish – may also be included as part of the employment (up to a maximum of 20%).

The doctoral student will join the project AI Confidential: Emerging Forms of AI Chatbot Use for Emotional Support and Personal Well-being Among Young Swedes, funded by the Swedish Research Council (Grant No. 2026-00497). The project explores how young people (aged 15–18) interpret and relate to AI as a conversational partner in personal areas of life, as well as the opportunities and challenges that traditional healthcare providers experience in relation to this development. The doctoral student is expected to plan and conduct empirical studies within the project, drawing on an existing collaboration with the Youth Guidance Centres in Sweden’s Västmanland Region and working in close collaboration with the research team.

The project is led by Matilda Tudor (PI), Media and Communication Studies, and Lina Eklund (co-PI), Human-Computer Interaction; both have research profiles in critical digital media studies and everyday automation. Read more about the project here.

jobs.title: PhD student in hydrology - wildfires effect on Arctic water cycle
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Earth Sciences
jobs.description_html:
PhD student in hydrology with a focus on wildfires effect on Arctic water cycle

Are you interested in working on cutting-edge research in hydrology, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at Uppsala University.

The Department of Earth Sciences is Sweden´s most comprehensive academic environment for research and education in geoscience. It offers a broad range of expertise that can contribute to solving important societal issues.

Earth is a dynamic and constantly changing planet. To understand how this planet works, our researchers seek answers in the field, through laboratory experiments and advanced models. Our research and education cover a wide range of disciplines, including rocks and minerals, weather and climate, the evolution of life, natural disasters, wind power and energy, environmental and water engineering, and sustainable development.

Our research combines natural sciences and technology with social sciences and is often interdisciplinary. More than 300 people from over 30 countries work at the department, both in Uppsala and at Campus Gotland.

Our six research divisions:

• Geophysics • Air, Water and Landscape Science • Mineralogy, Petrology and Tectonics • Natural Resources and Sustainable Development • Palaeobiology • Wind Energy For more information see: www.uu.se/earthsciences

The successful candidate will be enrolled in the Air, Water and Landscape Science programme (LUVAL). The position includes close collaboration with researchers at Uppsala University, SMHI and SLU, offering opportunities for interdisciplinary research, international networking, and engagement with societally relevant climate and environmental challenges.

Project description

The Arctic is rapidly warming, leading to changes in freshwater systems through melting glaciers, thawing permafrost, and shifting hydrological regimes. Understanding how these changes affect runoff generation, evapotranspiration, river discharge, and freshwater availability is a key challenge for Arctic hydrology. At the same time, wildfires activity is increasing across large parts of the Arctic, creating an additional disturbance that can alter vegetation, soils, permafrost conditions, and water flow paths.

This PhD project will investigate how climate change and increasing wildfire activity are reshaping the Arctic water cycle. By combining Earth Observation (EO) satellite data with large-scale hydrological modelling, the doctoral student will study the impact of various wildfire-related landscape changes on hydrological processes in Arctic drainage basins. The project will generate new knowledge regarding the drivers and controls of hydrological changes in the Arctic and contribute to an improved understanding and better predictive models for future freshwater resources in northern regions.

Duties
The doctoral work consists of investigating how climate change and increasing wildfire activity affect hydrological processes across the Arctic. Duties include analysis of Earth Observation and hydrological data, hydrological modelling, and statistical analyses, as well as writing scientific articles. The PhD student will work with hydrologists from Uppsala University, SMHI and SLU, and is expected to contribute to the overall progress of the project.

The doctoral education comprises four years of full-time studies, including courses and independent research. The applicant will also have the opportunity to participate in teaching, supervision, and other departmental duties, which may extend the employment by up to a maximum of 20%.

Requirements

To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must

  • hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in Hydrology, Physical Geography, Geosciences, Environmental Sciences, Environmental engineering or another relevant subject,
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

Applicants must fulfill the above requirements before the admission can be started. You must also have good oral and written proficiency in English, strong quantitative and analytical skills, and experience in processing and analysing environmental or geospatial data. The position requires basic programming skills for scientific data analysis, the ability to work both independently and as part of a team, and a strong interest in hydrology and environmental change. Great emphasis will be placed on personal qualities such as analytical ability, initiative, creativity, flexibility and problem-solving skills.

Additional qualifications

Experience with hydrological modelling, remote sensing, GIS, and programming (e.g., Python or R) is considered an advantage. Knowledge of Arctic environments, cold-region hydrology, or wildfire impacts on ecosystems and water resources is meritorious.

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University´s rules and guidelines.

jobs.department: Uppsala universitet, Medicinska och farmaceutiska vetenskapsområdet, Medicinska fakulteten, Institutionen för medicinsk cellbiologi
jobs.description_html:
Doktorand inom immunofysiologi

Institutionen för medicinsk cellbiologi vid Uppsala universitet är en stark och internationell forskningsmiljö. Institutionen har över 110 anställda varav ungefär 25 är doktorander, 10 postdoktorer, och 40 forskare, lärare och professorer.

Professor Mia Phillipsons forskargrupp är en internationell, dynamisk och mycket framgångsrik forskargrupp med ett väletablerat samarbetsnätverk och stark finansiering. Den forskning som bedrivs syftar till att avslöja nya roller för immunceller och att hitta sätt att reglera deras specifika funktioner i miljöer som sträcker sig från organutveckling och reglering av homeostas till läkning av vävnader, angiogenes och inflammation. Flera av de projekt som initierats i Professor Mia Phillipson laboratorium är nu i klinisk utvecklingsfas efter att ha överförts till läkemedelsutvecklingsbolag. Laboratoriet är utrustat med eller har tillgång till avancerade tekniska verktyg och teknik.

Projektbeskrivning
Doktorandprojektet syftar till att identifiera cellulära och molekylära mekanismer som skiljer regenerativ läkning från fibrotisk vävnadsreparation genom att jämföra två organ med fundamentalt olika skadeutfall: endometriet och hjärtmuskeln. Studierna kommer att använda tekniker som möjliggör detaljerade studier på encellsnivå, och ska genomföras i laboratoriemöss samt i en gnagare med unika läkningsförmågor, den afrikanska taggmusen (Acomys spp.). Genom att kombinera modeller för hjärtinfarkt och endometrie-fibros med encellssekvensering och detaljerad vävnadskarakterisering syftar projektet till att identifiera bevarade cellulära program som avgör om skadad vävnad läker eller utvecklar fibros.

Forskarutbildningen omfattar fyra års heltidsstudier. Andra arbetsuppgifter vid institutionen för medicinsk cellbiologi som avser utbildning och administrativt arbete kan förekomma (max 20%), vilket i så fall förlänger anställningen med motsvarande tid.

Kvalifikationskrav
Den blivande doktoranden ska ha: Akademisk grundexamen, t.ex. magisterexamen, inom ett relevant område, t.ex. immunologi, endokrinologi, mikrobiologi, molekylärbiologi, cellbiologi eller fysiologi. Utmärkta kunskaper i engelska i tal och skrift.

Vi söker en mycket motiverad doktorand som är entusiastisk över att både leda projekt och samarbeta i gruppens övriga projekt. I urvalsprocessen kommer tonvikt läggas på tidigare arbete i laboratoriemiljö och forskningserfarenhet inom fysiologi, molekylärbiologi, och mikrobiologi, samt dokumenterad erfarenhet av följande tekniker: mushantering, sövning och dissektion, cellmolekylära metoder, avancerad flödescytometri, samt avbildningstekniker, såsom intravital konfokal mikroskopi. Personliga kvalifikationer kommer att vara av stor betydelse i utvärderingsprocessen.

Ansökan bör innehålla en kort beskrivning av forskningsintressen och relevanta erfarenheter, CV, kopior av examensbevis och utskrifter samt den sökandes avhandling (eller ett utkast). Om möjligt, skicka också in referensbrev eller kontaktuppgifter till tidigare forskningshandledare.

Bestämmelser för doktorander återfinns i Högskoleförordningen 5 kap §§ 1-7 samt i universitetets regler och riktlinjer.

Ansökningsförfarande
Ansökan bör vara skriven på engelska och ska innehålla en meritförteckning, vetenskapliga publikationer, och ett personligt brev med kort beskrivning av dig själv, dina kunskaper och forskningsintressen samt namn, e-postadress och telefonnummer till två referenspersoner. Du bör även bilägga kopior av relevanta examensbevis och kursutdrag. Ansökningarna bedöms enligt behörighet, personlig lämplighet och tidigare erfarenhet av forskning inom närliggande områden.

Om anställningen
Anställningen är tidsbegränsad, enligt HF 5 kap § 7. Omfattningen är heltid. Tillträde enligt överenskommelse. Placeringsort: Uppsala

jobs.title: PhD student in laser spectroscopy
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Physics and Astronomy
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in working with femtosecond lasers and their application to liquid-phase chemical reactions, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a doctoral position at Uppsala University.

The research conducted at the Department of Physics and Astronomy encompasses a wide range of physics topics, distributed over nine divisions. The department is located in the Ångström laboratory and employs nearly 400 people, 100 of whom are doctoral students. It offers a broad physics curriculum to undergraduate and graduate students, participation in nationally and internationally leading projects for researchers, and opportunities for partnership with industry and various outreach activities. Read more on www.uu.se/physics.

The research will be conducted in the research program for Chemical and Bio-Molecular Physics at the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Uppsala University, which focuses on understanding the fundamental properties and ultrafast processes of matter at the atomic length and time scales of Ångströms and femtoseconds. The program has a leading position in the use of X-rays for probing atoms, molecules and chemical and biomolecular systems. We develop and apply novel X-ray methods and instrumentation and aim at revealing how the properties of a system result from its electronic structure and dynamics with applications in environmental, biophysical and chemical systems.


Duties
The PhD student will perform femtosecond laser spectroscopy experiments in the HELIOS laser laboratory operated by the division of X-ray Photon Science at Uppsala University. The goal is to study the charge dynamics during liquid-phase chemical reactions relevant to fields like light-harvesting and bond activation. The PhD student will contribute to the development of novel femtosecond THz and optical spectroscopy infrastructure and will design, execute, and analyze experiments aimed at understanding how molecular charge distributions drive chemical reactivity in catalysis. Additional responsibilities of the PhD student include the writing of scientific manuscripts, presentation of research findings at internal meetings and international conferences, as well as the active participation in collaborations with other experimental and theoretical groups.

Are you interested in probability theory, statistics, and mathematical modelling? Would you like to develop new methods for uncertainty quantification and apply these methods to large-scale clinical cancer data? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favorable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at the Department of Information Technology, Uppsala University.

The Department of Information Technology holds a leading position in both research and education at all levels. We are currently Uppsala University's third largest department, have around 350 employees, including 120 teachers and 120 PhD students. Approximately 5,000 undergraduate students take one or more courses at the department each year. You can find more information about us on the Department of Information Technology website.

At the Division of Systems and Control, we develop both theory and concrete tools to design systems that learn, reason, and act in the real world based on a seamless combination of data, mathematical models, and algorithms. Our research integrates expertise from machine learning, optimization, control theory, and applied mathematics, spanning diverse application domains such as medicine, energy systems, biomedical systems, neuroscience, and safety and security. The Division of Systems and Control enjoys a wide network of strong international collaborators all around the world, for example at the University of Oxford, the University of Melbourne, and the University of California, Los Angeles. We strive for all PhD students to get a solid international experience during their PhD.

About the DDLS Fellows program 
The PhD position is part of the national research programme DDLS.

Data-driven life science (DDLS) uses data, computational methods and artificial intelligence to study biological systems and processes at all levels, from molecular structures and cellular processes to human health and global ecosystems. The SciLifeLab and Wallenberg National Program for Data-Driven Life Science (DDLS) aims to recruit and train the next generation of data-driven life scientists and to create globally leading computational and data science capabilities in Sweden. The program is funded with a total of 3.3 billion SEK over 12 years from the Knut and Alice Wallenberg (KAW) Foundation.

In 2026 the DDLS Research School will be expanded with the recruitment of 25 academic and 7 industrial PhD students. During the course of the DDLS program more than 260 PhD students and 200 postdocs will be part of the Research School. The DDLS program has four strategic research areas: cell and molecular biology, evolution and biodiversity, precision medicine and diagnostics, epidemiology and biology of infection. For more information, please see: https://www.scilifelab.se/data-driven/ddls-research-school/

The future of life science is data-driven. Will you be part of that change? Then join us in this unique program!

At Uppsala University, we are announcing the position as DDLS PhD student in data-driven precision medicine and diagnostics.

Data-driven precision medicine and diagnostics covers data integration, analysis, visualization, and data interpretation for patient stratification, discovery of biomarkers for disease risks, diagnosis, drug response and monitoring of health. The precision medicine research is expected to make use of existing strong assets in Sweden and abroad, such as molecular data (e.g. omics), imaging, electronic health care records, longitudinal patient and population registries and biobanks. 

Project description
Data-driven mathematical and statistical models are increasingly used in life science research and healthcare. Quantifying the uncertainty associated with these models is crucial for understanding their reliability and for making informed decisions based on their predictions. This project aims to develop new methods for uncertainty quantification in mathematical and statistical models. The methods will be applied to large-scale clinical cancer data. A central application will be quantifying uncertainty in information extracted from medical reports and propagating this uncertainty into downstream probabilistic time-to-event models.

We are looking for candidates with:

Additional qualifications

jobs.title: PhD student in experimental nuclear physics with a focus on neutron-induced reactions
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Physics and Astronomy
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in working with experimental nuclear physics, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at Uppsala University.

The research conducted at the Department of Physics and Astronomy encompasses a wide range of physics topics, distributed over nine divisions. The department is located in the Ångström laboratory and employs nearly 400 people, 100 of whom are doctoral students. It offers a broad physics curriculum to undergraduate and graduate students, participation in nationally and internationally leading projects for researchers, and opportunities for partnership with industry and various outreach activities. Read more on www.uu.se/physics.

The Department of Physics and Astronomy, Division of Applied Nuclear Physics, at Uppsala University conducts research and education in applied nuclear physics. Its activities aim to deepen our understanding of the properties of atomic nuclei and apply this knowledge in areas such as energy and materials research.

The successful candidate will join a research group with a strong international profile and active collaborations at leading research facilities, including GANIL (France), JRC-Geel (Belgium), CERN n_TOF (Switzerland), GSI (Germany), and JYFL (Finland). The group’s research focuses on advancing our understanding of nuclear-reaction dynamics, with particular emphasis on neutron-induced reactions.

Through dedicated experiments, the research group produces high-precision nuclear data that extend beyond current experimental limits. These results contribute to the development of state-of-the-art nuclear-reaction models and evaluated nuclear-data libraries, supporting safe, reliable, and competitive technologies for both existing and future nuclear-energy systems, as well as societal applications in cancer treatment, radiation-tolerant microelectronics, and other radiation-based technologies.

Duties
The doctoral project will investigate the competition between different reaction mechanisms governing light-ion emission in neutron-induced reactions over a broad range of neutron energies. Particular attention will be given to the transition from compound-nucleus-dominated behaviour to pre-equilibrium and direct-reaction dynamics. The measurements will produce new high-precision nuclear data, including total production cross-sections and the energy and angular distributions of emitted light ions as functions of neutron energy. These results will advance the understanding and modelling of nuclear reactions and contribute to improving evaluated nuclear-data libraries.

The project also has important applications for structural materials used in nuclear installations and other irradiation environments. In future fusion devices and fast reactors, light-ion emission can lead to gas production and bubble formation, potentially affecting the mechanical properties and service life of structural materials.

As a doctoral student, you will conduct a substantial part of your experimental research at GANIL in Caen, France, one of the group’s principal international partner facilities. The project will focus on experiments at the Neutrons for Science facility, NFS, using its white-neutron beam to investigate light-ion emission in neutron-induced reactions.

A central part of your work will involve the Medley experimental setup, which was originally developed by the research group and is now permanently installed at GANIL. You will contribute to the simulation, preparation, optimisation, and further development of the experimental setup and its associated systems. You will also take an active role in preparing and carrying out measurement campaigns at GANIL, working closely with researchers and technical specialists at NFS.

Following the experiments, you will be responsible for analysing the collected data and interpreting the results using nuclear-reaction codes such as TALYS. By comparing the experimental findings with model calculations, you will assess the ability of current models to describe light-ion emission, particularly during the pre-equilibrium stage of the reaction. The results are expected to support the further development and validation of nuclear-reaction models.

The position requires extended research visits to GANIL and may include visits to other international facilities. You will communicate your research through scientific publications and presentations at national and international conferences.

Requirements
To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must

  • hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in physics, engineering physics, nuclear engineering, applied physics, or another area relevant to the project, or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.


The position also requires:

  • good knowledge of physics, including nuclear physics and radiation detection,
  • some programming experience, for example in Python, C++, and an interest in further developing these skills,
  • the ability to work independently and in a structured manner;
  • good collaboration skills,
  • good oral and written communication skills in English,
  • availability and willingness to undertake research visits abroad, including extended stays and shorter trips, primarily to GANIL, and to attend scientific conferences.

 

Additional qualifications

Experience in one or more of the following areas is considered a merit:

  • data analysis using ROOT,
  • particle-transport simulations using Monte Carlo codes such as Geant4, FLUKA, or OpenMC,
  • nuclear-reaction calculations using codes such as TALYS,
  • practical experience with radiation detectors, detector electronics, or data-acquisition systems,
  • theoretical modelling in nuclear physics,
  • scientific computing involving large datasets from simulations or measurements, including the use of high-performance computing resources.

jobs.title: PhD student in electrical engineering with focus on power system adequacy
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Electrical Engineering
jobs.description_html:
Electrification and digitalisation are among the major areas for the future transition to sustainable societies. The Department of Electrical Engineering conducts successful research and education in these areas - including renewable energy sources, electric vehicles, industrial IoT, 6G communication, and wireless sensor networks, as well as research and education in Life Science, health technology, smart electronic sensors, and medical systems. The Department of Electrical Engineering is an international environment with around 160 employees who contribute to important technological energy and health at the Ångström Laboratory.

We are now looking for a PhD student in electrical engineering with focus on power system adequacy.

Come and join us!
The position is placed at the Division of Electricity within the Department of Electrical Engineering. Here you will find a welcoming working environment with an active doctoral student network and a variety of experimental projects. The division collaborates with Swedish companies – both public and private – as well as other stakeholders within the various research areas. We look forward to receiving your application. Join us in building the future!

Read more about our benefits and what it is like to work at Uppsala University

Project description
Large dependencies of reliable power production from offshore renewable energy systems (RES) is expected in the next decades, in particular onshore and offshore wind and solar PV. Large changes are also seen in energy and electricity supply from non-renewable sources, due to, e.g., recent national policy changes around nuclear power or imported gas and oil. The demand side is transforming as well, driven by changes such as the electrification of transportation and other sectors, and increased use of heat pumps or air conditioning.

Finally, climate change is implying changes in weather, with heat waves and other weather extremes affecting society and the energy system. There are large knowledge gaps regarding the power production reliability under severe weather conditions and transforming energy systems. In this project, the student will investigate the security of electricity supply in the European power system in current and future projected scenarios considering transformations in the energy production, energy consumption, and climate.

The project is part of the Centre for Natural Disaster Science (CNDS), a national research centre that aims to prevent and improve society's preparedness for risks by increasing knowledge of the dynamics and consequences of natural disasters. Cooperation and communication within the CNDS network provide an interdisciplinary platform for exchanging expertise in natural disasters and risk reduction.

The research group at Uppsala University has extensive experience of research in electrical engineering and has a large laboratory activity. We offer a varied and exciting work, planned by the doctoral student and the research group together. The doctoral student will be supervised by at least two supervisors.

Duties

Teaching and other departmental duties may be part of the position, to a maximum of 20% of the working hours.

  • hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in electrical engineering, energy systems engineering, engineering physics or similar, or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

Specify other skills, competencies, and qualities that are required for the position.

We place great emphasis on personal qualities such as strong motivation, good collaboration and communication skills with other researchers. You should be purposeful, structured and be able to work effectively both individually and in groups.

The candidate must have excellent communication skills in English and/or Swedish, both orally and in writing.

Good oral and written proficiencies in Swedish is a merit. Experience in numerical modelling and programming as well as experimental work is a merit Experience from industry is a merit
