We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at the Department of Information Technology, Uppsala University. 

The Department of Information Technology holds a leading position in both research and education at all levels. We are currently Uppsala University's third largest department, with 350 employees, including 120 teachers and 120 PhD students. Approximately 5,000 undergraduate students take one or more courses at the department each year. You can find more information about us on the Department of Information Technology website.

The position is hosted in a research environment which includes verification experts (Parosh Abdulla, Mohammed Faouzi Atig, Bengt Jonsson, Philipp Ruemmer, Kostis Sagonas, Wang Yi), as well as experts in programming languages (Johannes Borgström, Eva Darulova, Lars-Henrik Erikson, Sofia Ouhbi, Tjark Weber, Tobias Wrigstad). The department is known for both strong theoretical work as well as tool development in these areas (UPPAAL, Concuerror, Nidhugg and other tools), publishing in top conferences such as POPL, PLDI, ICALP and CAV. 

Project description
As both private and public investment in quantum computing continues to surge, the steady upscaling of quantum hardware (now reaching thousands of qubits) has resulted in increasingly sophisticated quantum software pipelines. Given the strategic use of quantum software (e.g. in security), there is an urgent need for verifying the trustworthiness of quantum programs at scale. Features of modern quantum programs such as Quantum Error Correction lead to hybrid quantum-classical architectures, resulting in new challenges for verification. Current tools and techniques do not offer the desired combination of scalability, automation and guarantees to verify such programs. The project aims to address this gap by combining techniques from classical verification and programming language theory with those for complex arithmetic, in order to contribute both theoretical insights and software artifacts advancing the state of the art in quantum program verification.

jobs.title: PhD student in Biochemistry
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics is mainly located with the other Departments of Chemistry and Life Sciences in the Arrhenius Laboratories for Natural Sciences, which are situated in the northern part of the University Campus at Frescati. Some 270 people of which about 60 are PhD students work at the Department, engaged in internationally highly recognised research covering a broad range of subjects. More information about us, please visit: the Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics.

Project description

Your studies in Biochemistry will be in the project "Structural studies of Botulinum neurotoxins".

The botulinum neurotoxins are the most toxic substances known; they are one million times more toxic than the cobra toxin. In spite of their extreme toxicity the toxins are used in the treatment of a variety of medical conditions. We use structural biology, mainly X-ray crystallography and single particle cryo-EM, and several other methods to investigate questions concerning the botulinum neurotoxins and their interactions with both receptors and the neuronal membrane itself.

Qualification requirements

In order to be admitted to postgraduate education, the applicant must have the general and specific entry requirements. The qualification requirements must be met by the time the applicant is admitted to the PhD program at the Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics.

You meet general entry requirements if you have completed a second-cycle degree, or completed courses equivalent to at least 240 higher education credits, of which 60 credits must be in the second cycle, or have otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere.

Specific entry requirements, for acceptance in the Biochemistry program the applicant must have passed courses within the first and second cycles of at least 120 credits in Biochemistry/Life Science, including at least 15 credits Biochemistry at the second cycle level and a Degree Project (thesis) also in Biochemistry of 30 credits.

jobs.title: PhD student in Sustainability Science
jobs.description_html:
Stockholm Resilience Centre (SRC) is a leading international centre in sustainability science at Stockholm University. The Centre advances scientific understanding of the dynamic interactions between people and nature in the biosphere, trains the next generation of sustainability researchers and leaders, and engages in collaborations with change agents. It is a joint initiative between Stockholm University and the Beijer Institute of Ecological Economics at the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. The SRC currently employs around 165 members of staff.

More information about us, please visit: Stockholm Resilience Centre.

The SRC aims to foster new generations of researchers and academic leaders through our Resilience Research School. The school equips students with a theoretical and practical foundation in Sustainability Science with a focus on resilience in social-ecological systems. Students are encouraged to develop new approaches that integrate methods and concepts from the social, natural and applied sciences. Emphasis is placed on developing student ability to define a problem, develop research methods, and communicate research findings within international scientific and science-policy discussions.

Project description

This PhD position is part of Mistra Finance to Revive Biodiversity, an interdisciplinary research programme hosted by the Stockholm Resilience Centre that investigates the relationships between biodiversity, nature, and the financial system. FinBio brings together researchers across sustainability science, ecology, economics, finance, and related disciplines with financial-sector and other societal partners to develop science-based, decision-relevant approaches for integrating nature into financial decision-making. The programme takes a systems perspective, examining both how finance influences nature and how changes in nature generate risks, resilience, and opportunities for economic and financial systems.

We seek an independent and highly motivated PhD candidate to contribute to the development of next-generation approaches for understanding and managing nature-related financial risks. The project is based on the recognition that nature is not only affected by economic activities, but also plays a critical role in shaping financial risks and opportunities for building long-term resilience. Degraded ecosystems can amplify climate-related hazards such as floods, droughts, wildfires, and pest outbreaks, while healthy ecosystems can reduce vulnerability and strengthen the resilience of both societies and economic systems.

The PhD research will focus on how nature-related risks and resilience can be integrated into financial decision-making, with particular emphasis on the real estate and agrifood sectors. The project will include systematically mapping of the mechanisms through which changes in nature influence economic activities and financial risks. Building on this foundation, the PhD candidate will develop research on how resilience perspectives can be incorporated into financial risk assessment to improve both the credibility and practical usefulness of nature-related risk analyses. The PhD will be a key member of FinBio’s research on risk and resilience which is led by Prof Beatrice Crona. The PhD research will develop a stronger scientific basis for understanding how ecological processes can amplify, transmit, or mitigate financial risks, and how these insights can be incorporated into financial risk assessment.

The PhD research will focus on the real estate and agrifood sectors as case studies to contribute to 1) scientific understanding of nature-related financial risk and resilience and 2) the development and testing of methods, models, and decision-support approaches that can be applied in financial practice. In the real estate domain, this will involve investigating how nature-related risks and nature-based solutions influence property valuation, credit assessment, and financial stability. Within the agrifood sector, the PhD candidate will analyze how investors, lenders, and companies can promote more sustainable and resilient supply chains through governance mechanisms, incentives, and the monitoring of relevant sustainability indicators.

The research is being conducted with FinBio partners, including various institutional investors, banks companies, and other societal stakeholders. The PhD candidate is therefore expected to contribute both to academic publications and to the development of practical methods, recommendations, and decision-support tools for the financial sector.

Applicants should have an academic background in a field such as sustainability science, economics, finance, geography, environmental science, systems analysis, or related disciplines. Please note that both general and specific entry requirements must be met for the application to be considered (see qualification requirements below). Experience with interdisciplinary research, literature reviews, policy analysis, or quantitative methods is considered an asset. Because the project operates at the interface between science and practice, candidates should also be interested in collaborating with non-academic stakeholders and translating scientific findings into practical applications.

This PhD project will be supervised by Professor Crona in close collaboration with Professor Garry Peterson, Dr. Megan Meacham, and Professor Fedra Vanhuyse. The student will collaborate with researchers at the Stockholm Resilience Centre, the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, and the international network of researchers participating in the FinBio project. The successful candidate will be employed by the Stockholm Resilience Centre and will be based in Stockholm.

Qualification requirements

In order to be admitted to postgraduate education, the applicant must have the general and specific entry requirements. The qualification requirements must be met by the time the applicant is admitted to the PhD program at the Stockholm Resilience Centre.

You meet general entry requirements if you have completed a second-cycle degree, or completed courses equivalent to at least 240 higher education credits, of which 60 credits must be in the second cycle, or have otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere.

Specific entry requirements for admission to postgraduate studies in Sustainability Science are that the applicant has a total of at least 30 credits, or equivalent, at advanced level in Natural Science, as well as a thesis of at least 30 credits at advanced level in a relevant subject, or equivalent knowledge.

Selection

The selection among the eligible candidates will be based on their capacity to benefit from the training. The following criteria will be used to assess this capacity:

  • Subject knowledge relevant to the research area, for example sustainability science, environmental science, economics, finance, resilience food systems, real estate, or related fields.
  • Ability to synthesize and integrate knowledge from multiple disciplines, such as ecology, climate science, economics, finance, and sustainability science.
  • Demonstrated capacity for systems thinking and analysis of complex social-ecological systems, including an understanding of feedbacks, dependencies, vulnerabilities, and resilience.
  • Quantitative analytical skills, for example statistical analysis, risk assessment, scenario analysis, or modelling of environmental and economic processes.
  • Ability to develop conceptual frameworks and models that structure complex relationships among nature, climate, resilience, and financial risk.
  • Excellent command of English, with strong written and oral communication skills.
  • The applicant's personal references.

In addition, the following qualifications are desirable and will be considered meritorious during the selection process:

  • Experience in policy or governance analysis, including how scientific insights can be translated into decision-support tools, regulatory frameworks, or investment processes.
  • Experience working with geographic or spatial data.
  • Experience conducting systematic literature reviews and evidence syntheses, including the ability to critically assess scientific evidence and identify knowledge gaps.
  • Knowledge of the real estate sector, food systems, or other nature-dependent industries.
  • Fluent Swedish is a valued merit.

Project description

Your studies in Biochemistry will be in the project "Mechanistic Studies of Bioenergetic Protein Complexes".

We search for outstanding PhD candidates (1-3) to join our ERC-Advanced Grant Project ‘bioEnergetic’, with a focus on mechanistic studies of bioenergetic protein complexes catalyzing biological energy conversion. The project is focused on how membrane-bound enzymes in respiratory chains capture redox energy, and catalyze long-range proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) reactions across biological membranes. The project has a special emphasis on electrical field effects in protein function, and how these effects are linked to the structure and dynamics of the protein complexes. The PhD candidate will closely work with other PhD students, postdocs and senior scientists in an interdisciplinary team within a large collaborative project.

jobs.description_html:
The Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics is mainly located with the other Departments of Chemistry and Life Sciences in the Arrhenius Laboratories for Natural Sciences, which are situated in the northern part of the University Campus at Frescati. Some 270 people of which about 60 are PhD students work at the Department, engaged in internationally highly recognised research covering a broad range of subjects. 

SciLifeLab (SciLifeLab) is a national center for molecular biosciences with a focus on health and environmental research. The center combines frontline technical expertise with advanced knowledge of translational medicine and molecular bioscience. SciLifeLab is a national resource hosted by Karolinska Institutet, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm University and Uppsala University. The center also collaborates with several other universities.

The employment will be placed at the Department of biochemistry and biophysics, at Stockholm university.

More information about us, please visit: the Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics..

Project description

Your studies in Bioinformatics will be in the project: "AI-driven Multiscale Modelling of Membrane Protein Complexes".

Cell membranes are highly organized assemblies of proteins and lipids whose structure and composition change during disease, drug exposure, and cellular stress, but current structural biology and AI methods largely treat membrane proteins one at a time and rarely capture how proteins, lipids, and glycans jointly shape membrane organization.

In this project, the PhD student(s) will develop deep-learning-based methods to build multiscale structural models of cell membranes, starting from erythrocyte and mitochondrial membranes. Building on our group’s work on AlphaFold-based prediction of protein complexes [1], the project will extend these approaches to (1) predict the structure and interactions of membrane protein complexes embedded in a lipid environment, (2) integrate experimental constraints from proteomics, glycoproteomics, structural mass spectrometry, and lipidomics generated by collaborating experimental groups into the modelling pipeline, (3) scale the predictions from individual protein complexes to the organisation of entire membranes, building on our work on assembling large complexes with AlphaFold and Monte Carlo tree search [2], and (4) compare membrane organization across cell types and conditions - drawing on our proteome-scale map of the human protein interaction network [3] - to identify conserved and disease- or drug-specific remodeling patterns. The project may also connect to work on AI-based prediction of drug transport across membranes, building on our studies of the structural evolution of membrane transporters [4].

The PhD student(s) will work at the interface of structural bioinformatics, machine learning, and membrane biology, in close collaboration with experimental groups in membrane biology and structural biology.

The Elofsson group is located at SciLifeLab, Stockholm University. Elofsson has worked on protein structure prediction, protein evolution and in particular membrane proteins for more than two decades, using machine learning and other computational techniques. Among the group’s most important contributions are methods for assessing the quality of protein models, as well as recent work on predicting protein-protein interactions and building large protein complexes. The group currently comprises seven PhD students, three postdocs, and five senior researchers, and collaborates closely with computational and experimental groups at SciLifeLab and internationally. Arne Elofsson is currently the co-director of CEMERAI. For more information see https://bioinfo.se/.

Representative recent publications relevant to this project are listed below.
[1] Bryant, P, Pozzati, G. & Elofsson, A. “Improved prediction of protein-protein interactions using AlphaFold2”. Nat Commun, 2022 Mar 10;13(1):1265
[2] Bryant P, Pozzati G, Zhu W, Shenoy A, Kundrotas P, Elofsson A. “Predicting the structure of large protein complexes using AlphaFold and Monte Carlo tree search”. Nat Commun. 2022 Oct 12;13(1):6028
[3] Burke, D.F., Bryant, P., Barrio-Hernandez, I., … Elofsson, A. “Towards a structurally resolved human protein interaction network”. Nat Struct Mol Biol 2023, 30(2):216-225
[4] Sudha, G., Bassot, C., Lamb, J., Shu, N., Huang, Y. & Elofsson, A. “The evolutionary history of topological variations in the CPA/AT transporters”. PLoS Comput Biol 2021, 17(9):e1009278

jobs.description_html:

Some 270 people of which about 60 are PhD students work at the Department, engaged in internationally highly recognised research covering a broad range of subjects. More information about us, please visit: the Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics.

Project description

Project title: "Multiplex chromatin technologies to understand human brain development".

We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student to develop new multiplex technologies for chromatin mapping and apply them to understand the gene regulatory principles underlying human brain development. The project aims to uncover how different chromatin modalities are coordinated as neural stem and progenitor cells give rise to the diverse cell types of the human brain with particular focus on human-specific molecular mechanisms. The student will develop and optimise molecular methods to measure multiple chromatin features in the same cells, building on our laboratory’s work in single-cell epigenomics. By applying these technologies to the developing human fetal brain and stem cell-based models, we will investigate how combinations of chromatin features relate to gene expression, lineage commitment and the establishment of cell identity.

The project combines technology development with an in-depth investigation of human brain biology. Experimental work will be closely integrated with bioinformatic analysis to examine how chromatin states change during development and identify regulatory principles shared across, or specific to, different neural lineages. The student will be involved in method development, experimental design, data generation and biological interpretation. The project is intended to be part wet-lab and part computational and can be partially tailored to the student’s background and interests. Training in both advanced molecular methods and bioinformatic data analysis will be provided.

The successful candidate will join the Laboratory for Single-Cell Epigenomics and Neurobiology, led by Dr. Marek Bartosovic at Stockholm University. Our lab develops single-cell and multimodal chromatin profiling methods and combines molecular biology, neurobiology and computational analysis to understand gene regulation in the developing brain. We offer an interdisciplinary and supportive research environment that encourages scientific curiosity, creativity and professional growth.

If you are enthusiastic about developing new technologies and using them to understand how the human brain develops, we encourage you to apply.

jobs.description_html:
The Department of Meteorology at Stockholm University (MISU) conducts research and education spanning the atmosphere, ocean and physical climate sciences. MISU offers educational programmes at the Bachelor's, Master's and PhD levels. Our research addresses fundamental questions concerning the dynamics, physics, chemistry and biogeochemistry of the atmosphere and ocean relevant to weather and climate. MISU strives toward a broad representation of research within our scientific domain.

We study questions originating from the deep ocean to the upper atmosphere and from the tropics to the poles. In this effort, we use and develop theory, statistical methods, and numerical models in close interplay with observations. We also develop and lead observational research using remote-sensing and in-situ measurements, including satellite missions and icebreaker expeditions to the Arctic.

The department has around 60 employees and is embedded in a larger research environment, including the Bolin Centre for Climate Research, the Baltic Sea Centre and the Swedish e-Science Research Centre. The department is highly international, with over half of our employees coming from outside Sweden and both Swedish and English are used as working languages. We welcome and value diversity in our working environment.

Read more about us here: Department of Meteorology.

Project description

Interactions between aerosol particles and clouds make a potentially important but highly uncertain contribution to the anthropogenic radiative forcing of climate. This project seeks to better understand the ways in which aerosol pollution changes liquid clouds. The PhD student may investigate this topic by testing a new theoretical framework that predicts that aerosol pollution strengthens the updrafts in shallow convective clouds, causing the clouds to become deeper and more reflective. The student may also investigate trends in Earth’s radiation budget caused by aerosol-cloud interactions over the satellite era. Research tasks may involve performing numerical simulations or analyzing satellite data.

Project description

Clouds and their responses to varying environmental conditions are particularly important determinants of current climate and future climate change. However, the resolution of a typical climate model is far too coarse to explicitly represent processes of relevance to cloud formation. Those processes therefore need to be parameterized, or represented as functions of large-scale state variables. Such sub-grid scale parameterizations are associated with large uncertainties, and are also  computationally expensive. 

This project focuses on novel ways to bridge between micro- and global scales, to improve climate model accuracy, efficiency and generalizability, and leverage modern computer architecture. We will explore the use of machine learning (ML) models trained on combinations of observational data and high-resolution simulations, as alternatives to empirical parameterizations of essential, unresolved sub-grid scale processes related to turbulence, cloud formation and aerosol-cloud interaction. The tasks will include deriving and training data-driven models, coupling them to a large-scale climate model, evaluating the results against observations and traditionally parameterized models, and using the ML-enhanced model to estimate climate-relevant quantities like cloud radiative effects and forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions. 

The work will be carried out in close collaboration with data scientists within the Swedish e-Science Research Centre, and contribute to development of methods with applicability also beyond climate science. The successful candidate will thereby develop their skills in atmospheric science and climate modelling, but also in data science and machine learning, and in communicating and collaborating within and across disciplines.

jobs.title: PhD Student in Theoretical Physics: Quantum Sensing with Anharmonic Systems
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Physics is located in the AlbaNova University Center and has approximately 230 employees, 250 students at undergraduate level and 80 graduate students. There are four research subjects within the postgraduate program: Physics, Theoretical Physics, Chemical Physics and Medical Radiation Physics. These subjects span over several research groups with different research activities. For information about the Department of Physics, see: www.fysik.su.se/english.

Project description

Subject: Theoretical Physics

We invite applications for a PhD position in the theory of quantum sensing at the Department of Physics (Fysikum), Stockholm University. The project will be carried out within the research group led by Sofia Qvarfort and will be based at Nordita as part of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology (WACQT). The successful candidate will join a collaborative and international research environment in quantum physics, as well as the WACQT graduate school, with opportunities to interact with both theoretical and experimental researchers.

Quantum sensing is a rapidly developing quantum technology that aims to exploit quantum effects to achieve enhanced precision in measurements of weak forces, accelerations, gravitational effects, and other physical parameters. Candidate platforms span a broad range, from individual atoms and superconducting devices to mechanical resonators operating in the quantum regime.

A central question in quantum sensing is what physical resources can provide a genuine sensing advantage, and under which realistic conditions that advantage survives. Improvements in sensitivity can arise through the preparation of non-classical quantum states, changes in the dynamics by which a parameter is encoded, suitable measurement strategies, or by connecting multiple sensors into distributed quantum sensing networks. Understanding the interplay between these mechanisms, particularly in the presence of noise and decoherence, remains an important theoretical challenge.

This PhD project will investigate fundamental limits and new protocols for quantum sensing using tools from mathematical physics, quantum information theory, open quantum systems, and quantum metrology. Possible research directions include nonlinear and anharmonic quantum dynamics, generation and use of non-Gaussian states, distributed quantum sensing, and the role of realistic measurements and environmental noise. The project will be motivated by experimentally relevant quantum technologies, with an emphasis on mechanical resonators in the quantum regime. An important goal is to identify which physical resources and protocols can lead to meaningful improvements in sensitivity under realistic experimental constraints.

We are looking for a curious and motivated candidate with a strong interest in theoretical quantum physics and an enthusiasm for learning new ideas and methods. We value creativity, careful scientific thinking, collaboration, and a willingness to discuss and develop ideas with others. Stockholm University and Nordita strives to provide an inclusive research environment with equal opportunities for all. The position offers opportunities to develop an independent research profile while working closely with the supervisor and other researchers at Stockholm University, Nordita, WACQT, and international collaborators. The candidate will have opportunities to attend international conferences and research visits and will be supported in developing their teaching and science-communication skills.

jobs.description_html:
The Department of Physics is located in the AlbaNova University Center and has approximately 230 employees, 250 students at undergraduate level and 80 graduate students. There are four research subjects within the postgraduate program: Physics, Theoretical Physics, Chemical Physics and Medical Radiation Physics. These subjects span over several research groups with different research activities. For information about the Department of Physics, see: www.fysik.su.se/english.

Project description

Subject: Chemical Physics

The theoretical description of X-ray induced electronic transitions in liquid solutions and solid materials is complicated by the strong influence of the environment and the dynamical response for core-excitations. Recently the development in high-resolution spectroscopy, in particular resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS), allows for detailed investigations of molecular interactions and electron-correlation. However, X-ray spectroscopy in condensed phase requires improvements in theoretical modelling for reliable interpretation of the experimental data. Depending on background and interests, you will primarily develop accurate methods either for treatment of X-ray induced transitions in extended systems using advanced embedding techniques or for the treatment of low energy excitation phonons and vibration.

You will work in a European collaboration involving theoretical and experimental groups, and be involved also in experiments. The project ”Theory Development for High-Resolution RIXS Experiments on Liquid Solutions and Solid Materials” is a collaboration with Prof. Marcella Iannuzzi (University of Zurich) and is financed by the Swiss National Science Foundation. Partner organisations include Dr. Teodoro Laino (IBM Research), Prof. Thorsten Schmitt (Paul Scherrer Institut), and Prof. Lothar Weinhardt (Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, KIT Light Source).

We seek a motivated and creative candidate with a strong collaborative mindset eager to learn new skills. The position offers opportunities for international collaborations and participation in international conferences. You will be supported in developing your science communication skills. You will develop an understanding in quantum chemistry and simulation techniques to accurately model photo-induced processes. You will work in the division of Chemical Physics at the Department of Physics, in which the research spans over a wide range of experimental and theoretical projects. jobs.title: PhD student in Atmospheric Sciences and Oceanography, focus on mixed-phase cloud processes
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Meteorology at Stockholm University (MISU) conducts research and education spanning the atmosphere, ocean and physical climate sciences. MISU offers educational programmes at the Bachelor's, Master's and PhD levels. Our research addresses fundamental questions concerning the dynamics, physics, chemistry and biogeochemistry of the atmosphere and ocean relevant to weather and climate. MISU strives toward a broad representation of research within our scientific domain.

We study questions originating from the deep ocean to the upper atmosphere and from the tropics to the poles. In this effort, we use and develop theory, statistical methods, and numerical models in close interplay with observations. We also develop and lead observational research using remote-sensing and in-situ measurements, including satellite missions and icebreaker expeditions to the Arctic.

The department has around 60 employees and is embedded in a larger research environment, including the Bolin Centre for Climate Research, the Baltic Sea Centre and the Swedish e-Science Research Centre. The department is highly international, with over half of our employees coming from outside Sweden and both Swedish and English are used as working languages. We welcome and value diversity in our working environment.

Read more about us here: the Department of Meteorology.

Project description

Clouds regulate how much sunlight reaches the Earth’s surface and how much thermal radiation escapes to space, which ultimately influences how hot or cold the planet is. How much each cloud cools or warms the Earth depends in part on its composition. Is it made up of liquid particles, ice particles, or both? How densely spaced and how large are these particles? The answers to these questions lie partially in the dynamics occurring within the cloud. Even clouds that look calm from the ground may generate motions strong enough to shake an airplane. These motions can form new cloud particles and combine or shatter existing ones. However, these motions are difficult to represent completely in computer models of the atmosphere and in laboratory experiments, and we have yet to understand their full impact. 

The PhD student will build this understanding using over 800 hours of wind and cloud particle measurements that have been recorded by specialized research aircraft during field campaigns run by government agencies in the US and Europe. Data have been collected over the midwestern US and the Caribbean, off the northwestern coast of Africa, between Australia and Antarctica, and in the vicinity of Svalbard. Quality-controlled versions of all data are already available, so analysis can begin at the project start.The PhD student will develop a detailed understanding of aircraft instrumentation through literature review and apply that expertise to the analysis of measurements from dozens of different aircraft-mounted instruments. All analysis will be done in Python. 

The scientific scope initially spans micrometer-scale cloud particles to the dynamical processes that affect clouds, including turbulent eddies and kilometer-scale atmospheric waves. Initial science questions are well defined and focus on identifying statistical relationships between cloud particle properties and cloud-scale dynamics, and investigating how these vary across cloud types and geographic regions.

After the initial stage, the project is more open-ended. The PhD student may choose to focus on the same micrometer–kilometer scales, or to make connections between these scales and the regional or global climate. They may also choose to branch into atmospheric modelling and/or to use machine learning to model observed relationships between cloud dynamics and cloud particles.

Qualification requirements

In order to be admitted to postgraduate education, the applicant must have the general and specific entry requirements. The qualification requirements must be met by the deadline for applications.

You meet general entry requirements if you have completed a second-cycle degree, or completed courses equivalent to at least 240 higher education credits, of which 60 credits must be in the second cycle, or have otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere.

The specific entry requirements comprise a minimum of 90 higher education credits in one of the subjects meteorology, oceanography, physics or chemistry, at least 15 higher education credits in mathematics, as well as an independent degree project of at least 15 higher education credits. Furthermore, English language proficiency equivalent to English 6/English Level 2 at upper secondary school is required. The specific entry requirements may also be met by those who have acquired equivalent knowledge through other means, either in Sweden or abroad.

General syllabus for doctoral studies in Atmospheric Sciences and Oceanography.

Selection

Selection from among applicants who meet the entry requirements shall be made with regards to their ability to benefit from the programme. That fact alone that an applicant is assessed to be able to receive credits for previous educational or professional/vocational activities to be credited to the educational programme may not give the applicant priority over other applicants in the selection process. Decisions on admission are made in accordance with the applicable delegation regulations.

The assessment criteria for admission to the postgraduate programme in atmospheric sciences and oceanography are familiarity with the theory and applications of the subject, subject knowledge relevant to the research project, the ability to express oneself orally and in writing, proficiency in English, analytical ability, creativity, initiative, independence and the ability to work collaboratively. Prior Python experience is desirable but not required. The assessment of the applicant’s ability in these respects are based on the relevance and results of completed higher education courses, the quality and scope of the independent project, references, interviews and a personal statement from the applicant describing their expectations of, and intentions regarding, the programme.

jobs.title: PhD student in Psychology
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Psychology is a creative and international workplace for research and education. The Department of Psychology conducts successful research in occupational and organisational psychology, clinical psychology, cognitive psychology, perception and psychophysics, personality, social and developmental psychology, psychobiology and epidemiology.

Our researchers publish regularly in international journals and actively participate as experts in the media. We collaborate extensively with external organisations and we have a constant exchange of visiting students and researchers from all over the world. As a researcher with us, you will have access to modern research infrastructure. We have a recording studio, advanced laboratories for sleep and sensory research, and large databases that enable complex studies over time. We also collaborate with the Stockholm University Brain Imaging Centre, offering state-of-the-art imaging technologies, including MRI, EEG and TMS.

For more information about us, please visit the Department of Psychology.

Project description

The doctoral position is part of an ambitious project aiming to establish a scientific foundation for chronomedicine in psychiatry, a field that seeks to use the body's internal biological clock to improve treatment effectiveness and functioning. Many psychiatric symptoms (e.g., anxiety), cognitive processes (e.g., attention), and stress-related physiology (e.g., cortisol secretion) vary substantially across the day, but it remains unclear to what extent these fluctuations are driven by the circadian system or behavioural and environmental factors such as light, sleep, food intake, and stress exposures.

To address this question, the doctoral student will contribute to several interconnected studies, including ecological momentary assessment (EMA) to track cognition, mood, stress, and physiology in everyday life, a highly controlled laboratory protocol known as constant routine to isolate endogenous circadian rhythms from external factors, and experimental studies examining circadian-timed cognitive probes.

The project offers an opportunity to work at the intersection of psychiatry, neuroscience, sleep and circadian biology, and stress research. The doctoral student will gain training in intensive longitudinal data collection, cognitive and physiological measurements, and advanced statistical methods. 

Qualification requirements

In order to be admitted to postgraduate education, the applicant must have the general and specific entry requirements. The qualification requirements must be met by the deadline for applications.

You meet general entry requirements if you have completed a second-cycle degree, or completed courses equivalent to at least 240 higher education credits, of which 60 credits must be in the second cycle, or have otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere.

The applicant must be able to engage with scientific literature written in English.

See the General Syllabus for Third-Cycle (Doctoral) Studies in Psychology.

Selection

In the selection process, consideration will be given to previous academic merits, and an assessment will be made of the applicant’s ability to benefit from the doctoral training programme. The main basis for this assessment is (1) the thesis/publication to be submitted with the application, and (2) other educational and professional qualifications, including previous publications (CV).

The project involves data collection, partly conducted during the evening and night in the sleep laboratory. Particular merit will be given to applicants with:

  • Experience working in a human sleep laboratory.
  • Experience working with intensive longitudinal study designs measuring stress physiology (e.g., HRV and wearable sensor technologies).
  • Experience with physiological measurements related to stress and autonomic function, such as heart rate variability (HRV) and wearable sensor technology.
  • Excellent English language skills, both written and spoken, as the candidate will be part of an international research environment.
  • Proficiency in Swedish, as the study involves interaction Swedish-speaking participants.

jobs.title: PhD student in English with Specialisation in Literary Studies
jobs.description_html:
The Department of English provides education at the bachelor's, master's, and doctoral levels, and is part of the Faculty of Humanities. The Department has a staff of about 35 people. There are approximately 750 registered students at undergraduate level.
More information about us, please visit: the Department of English.

Subject area

Research interests among our members of staff cover areas such as early modern literature, nineteenth-century literature, modernism, and twentieth-century and contemporary literatures, narratology and critical theory, with a strong profile in postcolonial and world literatures.

Qualification requirements

In order to be admitted to postgraduate education, the applicant must have the general and specific entry requirements. The qualification requirements must be met by the deadline for applications.

You meet general entry requirements if you have completed a second-cycle degree, or completed courses equivalent to at least 240 higher education credits, of which 60 credits must be in the second cycle, or have otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere.

Specific entry requirements are described in the general syllabus for doctoral studies in the field of English.

An applicant meets the specific eligibility requirements for doctoral studies in English if he or she has received a passing grade on course work of at least 30 ECTS credits in English at the advanced level (alternatively in linguistics or comparative literature), including a thesis of at least 15 ECTS credits.

Additionally, the applicant must document proficiency in English as measured by one of the following internationally recognised language proficiency tests: TOEFL iBT, TOEFL iBT Home Edition or TOEFL iBT Paper Edition with a minimum of 102 (and 27 in Writing); Cambridge C1 Advanced with a minimum Grade B (and B in Writing); IELTS Academic, IELTS Online or IELTS UKVI (Academic) with a minimum of 7.5 (and 7.0 in Writing); Pearson PTE Academic or PTE Academic Online with a minimum of 76 (and 82 in Writing).

Selection

The selection among the eligible candidates will be based on their capacity to benefit from the training. The following criteria will be used to assess this capacity:

  • Documented knowledge in a relevant field of research
  • Capacity for analytical and creative thinking
  • Initiative
  • Independence
  • Ability to collaborate
  • Written and oral proficiency in English
  • Availability of supervision.

Admission Regulations for Doctoral Studies at Stockholm University.

About the employment

We offer a fixed-term employment as a doctoral student according to Chapter 5 of the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100). The period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for four years. As a doctoral student, you should primarily devote yourself to your own doctoral education, but the employment may include work with education, research and administration to a limited extent (maximum 20 %).

A new employment as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, the employment is then renewed for a maximum of two years at a time.

Stockholm University strives to be a workplace free from discrimination and with equal opportunities for all.

Contact

For more information, please contact the Director of Graduate Studies Giles Whiteley, giles.whiteley@english.su.se.

Application

Apply for the PhD student position at Stockholm University's recruitment system. Attach a personal letter and CV as well as the attachments requested in the application form. It is the responsibility of the applicant to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the job advertisement, and that it is submitted before the deadline.

The instructions for applicants are available at: How to apply for a position.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in mathematics education
jobs.department: Karlstad University / Faculty of Health, Science and Technology / Department of Mathematics and Computer Science
jobs.description_html:
Are you a practicing teacher or a teacher education graduate with an interest in how teaching can be developed based on research? Would you like to further specialise in your subject while contributing to school development? Then a doctoral studentship within the graduate school BEPPE might be the next step in your professional career.

Karlstad University is now accepting applications for a doctoral studentship at the graduate school BEPPE. The doctoral student will be employed at the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science.

The graduate school on subject-specific education models in primary school (BEPPE)

The graduate school BEPPE aims to contribute to more systematic knowledge about how several scientifically established, yet mutually distinct, subject-specific education models function across different subjects and school contexts, and how they can be integrated into teacher education and primary education. As a doctoral student, you will conduct research on applied teaching practices in primary school, with a close connection to teacher education and school practice.

The graduate school is jointly organised by Karlstad University and the University of Gothenburg and currently has a total of nine doctoral students.

We welcome applications from teacher educators, schoolteachers, and from those who are otherwise interested in conducting research on teaching and learning within the advertised areas of specialisation. Applicants can be at an early stage of their careers – the key point is an interest in teaching, learning and school development in interaction with research. BEPPE offers a dynamic environment with opportunities to establish international networks, participate in conferences and engage in exchange programmes abroad. More information about the graduate school and its research (in Swedish): BEPPE.

Subject environments

The graduate school is a part of Karlstad University’s research environment focusing on subject-specific education. The research environment includes ROSE (Research on Subject-specific Education) and three research centres: CSL (Centre for Language and Literature Education), CSD (Centre for Social Science Didactics ) and SMEER (Science, Mathematics and Engineering Education Research). The subject-specific education perspective involves a particular interest in teaching and learning within specific subjects or subject areas. As a doctoral student in mathematics education, you will be affiliated with SMEER.

Duties

As a doctoral student, you will primarily dedicate time to your own studies. The doctoral programme comprises 240 credits for a Degree of Doctor and 120 credits for a Degree of Licentiate. The doctoral appointment is a paid position that offers a combination of studies and work, and a great opportunity for a potential career in academia. Doctoral students are expected to work independently and be prepared to contribute to the activities and development of the discipline and the department. You are given the opportunity to deepen your interests in collaboration with others. Teaching and administrative duties may also be included upon agreement but will not constitute more than 20% of full-time. Work as a doctoral student allows for great freedom and flexibility in terms of how you organise your tasks. This requires commitment, drive, and the ability to structure your work to successfully complete the doctoral thesis.

To contribute to a positive work environment and further both the department's activities and your own development as a researcher, we expect you to be a present and active part of the day-to-day operations and workplace community, whether working remotely or on site.

Entry requirements and admission

To be eligible for a doctoral studentship, applicants must meet the general and specific entry requirements (Higher Education Ordinance, Chap. 7, Sect. 35).

To meet the general entry requirements, applicants must have been awarded a second-cycle qualification, satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance, Chap. 7, Sect. 39).

To meet the specific entry requirements for third-cycle education in mathematics with a specialisation in mathematics education, the applicant must hold a Degree of Master (60 or 120 credits) that includes courses in mathematics and mathematics education corresponding to at least 90 credits, including a degree project (independent project) of at least 15 credits with relevance to third-cycle education, alternatively have a Bachelor or Master of Education, or equivalent qualifications according to previous programme requirements, with a specialisation in mathematics.

An applicant can also meet the specific entry requirements by in some other way having acquired equivalent prerequisite knowledge, in Sweden or abroad. Applicants who have not completed 90 credits in mathematics but have acquired equivalent prior knowledge in another way may be subject to an equivalence assessment.

To be eligible for doctoral studies, applicants must also be considered to have the ability required to benefit from the programme (Higher Education Ordinance, Chap. 7, Sect. 35). Admission is based on individual assessment.

Assessment criteria

The assessment of eligible applicants is based on the criteria listed below.

Special weight will be given to:

  • Results from previous studies
  • The quality of independent written work of a scholarly and investigatory nature included in the previous studies, particularly at master’s level and within mathematics education
  • Completed teacher education or other pedagogical education of similar scope, as well as experience as a teacher
  • At least 2 years of professional experience as a teacher, including mathematics education

Considerable weight will be given to:

  • Research plan and its relevance to the focus areas of the graduate school
  • The extent to which the applicant is able to be a physically present and active member of the research environment of the subject
  • Personal qualities such as the ability to work independently, demonstrate strong collaboration skills, a structured approach and effective oral communication

Weight will be given to:

  • Proficiency in Swedish and English (the doctoral studies will be conducted in a Swedish context, and data may include spoken and written content in Swedish)

Terms

Upon admission to doctoral studies, the person will be offered the appointment of doctoral student (Higher Education Ordinance, Chap. 5, Sect. 3). The position comprises four years of full-time studies consisting of research only. If teaching or other departmental duties become relevant, the appointment will be extended by a corresponding period, up to a maximum of five years full-time. The position is fixed-term, one year initially, followed by possible extensions of a maximum of two years at a time (Higher Education Ordinance, Chap. 5). Start date as agreed by both parties.

The salary for the doctoral studentship corresponds to the standard level of salary for doctoral students and progresses in accordance with a local collective agreement.

Application

Submit the application via the University’s web-based recruitment tool, Varbi. Applicants are responsible for submitting a complete application in accordance with the advertisement, for providing translations of any documents written in a language other than Swedish, Norwegian, Danish or English, and for ensuring that the documentation allows for objective and qualitative assessments. A complete application should be submitted by the application deadline. An incomplete application may jeopardise a fair assessment of qualifications. The application should include:

  • A cover letter where the applicant details the reasons behind their interest in the position
  • Brief research plan: The plan should include problem statement, purpose, theory and method, and will serve as a basis for assessing suitability for doctoral studies (1,000-2,500 words). However, it does not necessarily have to be linked to the future research project.
  • An account of language skills
  • A list of qualifications (CV)
  • Degree certificate with a complete transcript of the courses included, or a certified list of completed courses with grades and dates
  • Copy of master’s thesis (60 or 120 credits) or similar
  • Where applicable, copies of publications or certificates for other qualifications
  • Any letters of recommendation
  • Two references, such as a teacher, supervisor, or former or current manager

Attach all the documents and publications you wish to be considered to the electronic application (do not just provide links). Name each uploaded document to clearly indicate its content.

Documents that cannot be submitted electronically should be sent to the following address:

Karlstads universitet
HR-avdelningen
HR-administratör
651 88 KARLSTAD
SWEDEN

Application deadline: October 21, 2026

State the reference number: REK2026/230

Applicants with qualifications from abroad

If you have qualifications from a university outside Sweden or if they have not been recognised by a Swedish authority before, it is important that you attach degree certificates and official transcripts to facilitate the recognition of foreign qualifications.
Provide a contact for the degree-awarding institution (phone number or email) who can verify your qualifications.

We look forward to your application!

Karlstad University has chosen advertising channels for this recruitment and firmly declines any contact with advertising or recruitment agencies.

jobs.title: Doctoral Student in Psychology
jobs.department: Department of Psychology and Social work
jobs.description_html:
Job description
The research project is at the intersection of social psychology and sociolinguistics, examining how accents function as social signals. The focus is on social perception, attitudes, emotions, and behaviours related to foreign accents.

The research addresses questions of stereotypes, discrimination, and social inclusion from a Swedish and international perspective, with a consistent gender perspective throughout. The project is interdisciplinary and connects to work and organisational psychology, political science, gender studies, and research on integration and belonging.

Methodologically, the project is primarily based on experimental studies and psychometric approaches, with the possibility of applying neuroscientific methods as well.

The position is within the Department of Psychology, which is characterised by a close and personal environment with strong collegial support. The doctoral student will be part of an interdisciplinary and internationally oriented research environment and will work in close collaboration with supervisors, with considerable emphasis on developing independence in planning, implementation, and scientific communication. In the later stages of the dissertation, the doctoral student may have the possibility to design their own sub-study within the project's overarching themes.

The position involves doctoral studies, comprising research (80%) and teaching and administrative work (20%). The primary duties consist of conducting supervised research leading to a doctoral dissertation. The position also includes completing 60 higher education credits in doctoral courses, as well as participating in seminars and other activities within the subject area and the department. 

 

Entry requirements
General entry requirements include a second-cycle level qualification, or fulfilment of courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits must be at second-cycle level, or the equivalent knowledge gained in some other way in Sweden or abroad. Specific entry requirements include at least 90 credits in the subject of psychology or the equivalent knowledge gained in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

 

Other Requirements
Strong English skills, both spoken and written, are required. Good knowledge of Swedish or another Scandinavian language (Norwegian or Danish) is an asset.

The applicant must be driven and independent, analytical, initiative-taking, collaborative, development-oriented, and persistent.

Higher education at the advanced level in psychology, as well as prior experience in the project's research area, are assets for the position. Experience in developing or validating psychometric tools, working with EEG/ERP or other neuroscientific methods, and knowledge of tools such as R, MATLAB, or Python are also considered assets. A scientific publication or manuscript in progress may be considered an asset, particularly if it relates to the project's research area.

 

Assessment criteria
Selection among eligible applicants is made on the basis of an overall assessment of the applicant's ability to successfully complete a doctoral education. The assessment will place particular emphasis on the scientific quality of independent degree projects, the project plan submitted with the application, the applicant's personal qualities, and the applicant’s understanding of and interest in the project's research area.

 

Employment process
Processing of the appointment will comply with the provisions in Chapter 5 of the Higher Education Ordinance (Högskoleförordningen, SFS 1993:100) and will be carried out in accordance with Mid Sweden University’s Employment Procedures.

 

Terms of employment 
The doctoral position corresponds to five years of employment and is expected to lead to a doctoral degree. In addition to doctoral studies, which comprise 80% of the full-time position, teaching and administrative work will make up the remaining 20%, making it equivalent to a full-time post. If the pace of study in doctoral education changes, the employment period will be adjusted accordingly.

Initial doctoral student positions are valid for a maximum of one year, after which the position may be renewed by no longer than two years at a time. Provisions regarding doctoral studentship employment can be found in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), Chapter 5, Sections 1-7. 

Start date: 2027-01-15 or as agreed

Place of employment: Östersund

Salary: In accordance with Mid Sweden University’s salary scale for doctoral student.

 

Information
For more information, contact the Head of department, Ulrika Danielsson, ulrika.danielsson@miun.se or 010-142 84 90, or the Project leader, Marie-France Champoux-Larsson, marila@miun.se or 010-142 85 38.

 

Application
Application documents must be submitted in Swedish or English.

A cover letter, CV, proof of completed degrees, undergraduate and advanced level theses, a project plan, and any scientific publication/manuscript in progress should be attached to the application.

The project plan (approx. 2 – 3 single-spaced pages excluding references) should present a possible research project within the scope of the position’s research area and must include a background to the research area, one or more research questions, a description of methods and research design, and a brief discussion of the project's relevance to the position. The project plan does not need to correspond to the final dissertation project, but is intended to give the applicant the opportunity to demonstrate their ability for scientific reasoning, research design, and critical thinking.

Qualifications cited in the application must be substantiated.

Please submit your application through our recruitment system no later than 2026-11-22.

jobs.title: Doctoral Students for the DIW Graduate Center PhD Program in Economics
jobs.institution: DIW Berlin - Deutsches Institut für Wirtschaftsforschung e.V.
jobs.description_html:
The DIW Graduate Center (GC) at the German Institute for Economic Research welcomes applications from highly qualified students from around the world to enroll in its structured doctoral program in Economics.

The goal of the DIW Graduate Center is to provide outstanding doctoral students with a research environment and a training structure that will allow their talents to fully develop. The program equips them with a deep understanding of economic and social processes while offering them the opportunity to apply their knowledge at the largest economic research institute in Germany.

We are looking for Doctoral Students for the DIW Graduate Center PhD Program in Economics The DIW Graduate Center offers a five-year program of in-depth training in Economics leading to a PhD from one of Berlin’s universities. Students will complete a rigorous coursework curriculum and receive on-the-job training in DIW Berlin’s research departments. Students' research may be theoretical or applied in nature. Most work at the GC, however, has a strong empirical component. The program also encourages funded internships at prestigious institutions such as the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank and government ministries, as well as research stays at renowned universities around the world.

The DIW Graduate Center offers five years of funding with a standard stipend of 1,650 euros per month in the first year and a work contract in subsequent years. After completing the first year, doctoral students will join one of the research departments at the institute.

Requirements: Applicants to our PhD program must hold a master’s degree or diploma in Economics. Applications may also be submitted while the degree is still in progress, provided it is completed before the program starts. Degrees from other related fields (such as statistics, quantitative social sciences, mathematics or engineering) may also fulfill requirements for the program if the applicant has a sufficient background in Economics.

Applicants whose native language is not English must demonstrate English language proficiency unless they hold a degree from a university in an English-speaking country or can document at least one year of studies in an English-speaking degree program. A high score on the TOEFL or IELTS test is considered sufficient evidence of English proficiency. Knowledge of German is not required for a successful application, but students are encouraged to learn German and improve their language skills over the course of the program

Application and Information: We value diversity and therefore welcome all applications—regardless of gender, disability, nationality, or ethnic and social background.

Please apply only online through our application portal by January 15, 2027, quoting the reference number GC-1-26-Stip-e and include the following application documents:

  • Motivation letter (max. 2 pages) explaining your reasons for applying and briefly outlining your major research interests;
  • Detailed curriculum vitae (without photograph);
  • Two academic letters of recommendation, to be submitted directly by senior academics (e.g., professors, postdoctoral researchers) via our application site;
  • Copies of academic transcripts and other certificates;
  • Completed application form (can be found on our application site);
  • IELTS or TOEFL scores, if applicable;
  • GRE General Test – Test Taker Score Report (PDF), if applicable. Please also attach your GRE Test if you have already submitted it to the Institutional Account.
You can access the application portal via our GC website under application site.

Please note that only applications submitted through the application portal will be considered and that the application is to be completed in English.

Do you have any questions about this call for applications or the online application? You may find your question already answered on our GC website, particularly in the FAQ section of the application site — please take a look before contacting us.

If you still have questions after reviewing our GC website, please contact gradcenter@diw.de for content-related inquiries and recruiting@diw.de for technical questions regarding the online application.

Founded in 1925, DIW Berlin (the German Institute for Economic Research) is one of the leading economic research institutes in Germany. The Institute analyzes the economic and social aspects of topical issues, formulating and disseminating policy advice based on its research findings. DIW Berlin is part of both the national and international scientific communities, provides research infrastructure to academics all over the world, and promotes the next generation of scientists. A member of the Leibniz Association, DIW Berlin is independent and primarily publicly funded.

jobs.title: PhD position on Physics-Guided Digital Twin Development for Composition-Process-Structure-Property Modeling of Magnesium Alloys
jobs.description_html: Cutting-edge Research for a Changing World PhD position on Physics-Guided Digital Twin Development for Composition-Process-Structure-Property Modeling of Magnesium Alloys Reference code: 1057 - 2026/WD 1 Commencement date: as soon as possible Work location: Geesthacht Application deadline: November 12th, 2026 The Institute of Material and Process Design at the Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon is offering a 4-year PhD position in the field of computational materials engineering, machine learning, and digital twins for advanced lightweight materials. The focus of the PhD project will be the development of a physics-guided digital twin framework for magnesium alloys by integrating experimental characterization, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, precipitation modeling, and machine learning approaches to establish quantitative composition-process-structure-property relationships. Building upon recently developed machine-learning approaches for structure-property prediction in extruded magnesium alloys, the project aims to advance toward a next-generation Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) framework capable of predicting microstructure evolution and resulting mechanical properties across previously unseen processing conditions and material states. The candidate will work closely with interdisciplinary teams combining expertise in magnesium alloy development, thermomechanical processing, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, machine learning, and advanced experimental characterization. The objective of the project is to bridge the gap between purely data-driven materials modeling and mechanistic microstructure simulations by combining crystal plasticity, dynamic recrystallization, precipitation kinetics, and machine learning into a unified digital-twin framework. The resulting methodologies shall enable accelerated alloy and process design by leveraging experimentally validated physics-guided surrogate models with improved extrapolation capabilities beyond the limits of conventional machine-learning approaches. This work directly contributes to the digital transformation of materials development and manufacturing technologies for future lightweight engineering applications. Equal opportunity is an important part of our personnel policy. We would therefore strongly encourage qualified women to apply for the position. jobs.description_html: registration number: fb17-0026-wmz-2026 Entry date: as soon as possible Application deadline: 2026-11-01 Salary: E 13 TV-H Duration: 3 years Volume of employment: part-time (65 %) The University of Marburg, founded in 1527, offers a variety of excellent programs of study for around 22,000 students and confronts the important topics of our time through excellent research across a broad spectrum of sciences. The Department of Biology and the Center for Synthetic Microbiology, research group “Bacterial Cell Biology-, Prof. Dr. Martin Thanbichler (PubMed), is currently accepting applications for a PhD position in Bacterial Cell Biology (doctoral research assistant) in the context of the Research Training Group Microbial Nucleotide Metabolism (GRK 2937), funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG). The position is limited to a duration of 3 years. The starting date is as soon as possible. Salary and benefits commensurate with a public service position in the state Hesse, Germany (TV-H E 13, 65 %). Nucleotides play a critical role in bacterial physiology, driving fundamental processes such as DNA/RNA biosynthesis, cell envelope biogenesis, and energy metabolism. The Research Training Group "Microbial Nucleotide Metabolism" (GRK 2937) aims to elucidate the molecular mechanisms mediating vital nucleotide-dependent processes. Furthermore, it provides doctoral candidates with a comprehensive, structured training program designed to equip them with a broad knowledge base and an advanced molecular microbiology skillset. Within this framework, the open PhD position focuses on the mechanisms driving bacterial DNA segregation. In particular, the successful candidate will investigate the mechanistic principles underlying the function and organization of the conserved ParAB_S_ partitioning system, using a combination of cell biological, genetic, biochemical, biophysical and computational approaches. These studies will shed light on fundamental principles of cellular organization in bacteria while preparing the candidate for a successful career in the life sciences. jobs.description_html:
At the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law, scholars pursue research relating tofundamental issues and current developments in the areas of public international law, European Union law, and the constitutional and administrative law of individual states, together with numerous visiting scholars from all over the world. In its fields, our library is the largest in Europe and one of the most comprehensive in the world.

The newly established Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER), headed by Dr. Gordon Friedrichs at the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg, invites applications for two Research Fellow positions (Doctoral Researchers) (x/f/m) with a preferred starting date of 1 January 2027 (the positions are funded for three years)
The Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER) investigates how global order istransformed as states - particularly great and middle powers - pursue competing visions of the principles, rules andinstitutions that structure international relations amid intensifying geopolitical rivalry. The group conceptualizes theseprocesses as constellations of global (dis)ordering through which states seek to advance their visions of order by creating,reshaping, connecting, bypassing, or disengaging from international institutions, building new formal or ad hoc institutionalarrangements, and strategically leveraging economic and technological interdependence. DISORDER examines how suchconstellations emerge across the fields of security, economy, and technology, and what forms of global order they produce,transform, or erode.

Job description The successful candidates will develop independent doctoral dissertation projects within the framework of the Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER). Their research should contribute to the group’s broader inquiry into how states pursue competing visions of global order through international institutions and how these processes reshape global order across different issue areas.

Possible orientations of the doctoral projects include:
  • an actor-centred perspective, examining how a particular great or middle power pursues its vision of global order across different issue areas institutional settings; or
  • a domain-centred perspective, comparing how different states interact with and reshape international institutions within aparticular field, such as security, economy, or technology
Potential empirical cases may include, but are not limited to, the United States, China, Russia, India, Brazil, Japan, and other international actors such as the European Union.

The doctoral researchers will:
  • develop and conduct an original PhD project that contributes to the conceptual and empirical agenda of the DISORDER research group;
  • conduct empirical research using qualitative methods such as process tracing, qualitative content and discourse analysis, and semi-structured interviews;
  • contribute to the comparative and collaborative research activities of the group;
  • participate in research group meetings, workshops, conferences, and other academic activities;
  • present research findings at international conferences and prepare publications for peer-reviewed academic outlets;
  • contribute to the organization of workshops, conferences, and other activities of the research group and the MPIL.
Your profile
  • An excellent Master’s degree or equivalent in Political Science, with a specialization in International Relations or Foreign Policy Analysis
  • A strong research interest in global order, international institutions, and great- and middle-power politics, including their foreign policies
  • A substantive interest in one or more of the group’s empirical issue areas (security, economy, and technology)
  • A strong interest in qualitative research and familiarity with relevant research methods
  • Excellent written and spoken English
  • Additional language skills and country- or region-specific expertise relevant to the proposed doctoral project are considered assets
  • The ability to conduct independent research while contributing actively to a collaborative research environm
We offer
  • An attractive and international work environment with an unparalleled research infrastructure and a good working atmosphere
  • A varied, responsible and team-orientated job
  • Remuneration in accordance with the guidelines of the MPG funding agreements (65 per cent of EG13, TVöD-Bund)
  • Access to our world-leading library and a multitude of databases
  • A workplace that is easy to reach by public transport and free employee parking spaces
  • A job ticket for public transport
  • Offers for work-life balance and four affiliated daycare centres
Application The Max Planck Society has set itself the goal of employing more severely disabled people. Applications from severely disabled persons are expressly encouraged. The Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. Furthermore, the Max Planck Society aims to increase the proportion of women in areas where they are underrepresented. Women are therefore strongly encouraged to apply.

Interested candidates are invited to submit their complete application exclusively via the online application system availableon our website by 22 November 2026.

Applications should include a CV, a cover letter of no more than two pages, copies of relevant degree certificates and transcripts of records, a one-page summary of the applicant’s Master’s thesis, a five-page PhD project proposal that clearlyrelates to the research agenda of the DISORDER group and indicates which of the thematic orientations outlined above the proposed project primarily addresses, and two letters of recommendation.

The documents will be deleted after the application process. The interviews will take place in late November/early Decemberin person at the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg. Application expensescannot be covered.

For questions regarding the positions, please contact Dr. Gordon Friedrichs at friedrichs@mpil.de.
