jobs.title: PhD Position Chaotic Sampling for Secure and Sustainable Networked Control Systems
jobs.description_html:
Engineers usually want predictability. This project embraces chaos! – Excited about control theory? Then join us to build the math of chaotic sampling for greener and more secure control systems.

Job description
Wireless communication can make control systems cheaper and easier to deploy, but bandwidth and energy limitations, as well as vulnerability to cyber-attacks, restrict its use in critical applications. Event-based control approaches can greatly reduce communication by transmitting information only when required, while potentially generating complex, chaotic sampling patterns. This project investigates how such patterns can be designed systematically to make communication timing difficult for an external observer to predict, while maintaining closed-loop stability and using network resources efficiently.

In this PhD project, you will develop mathematical theory and computational methods for the analysis and design of chaotic sampling mechanisms in networked control systems. You will study conditions under which event-based sampling exhibits chaotic behavior and how to design controller and sampler strategies that account for stability, communication rate, and measures of timing unpredictability such as entropy. You will also investigate the robustness of these mechanisms to disturbances and assess whether transmission patterns can be learned from external observations.

This position is part of a new lab at the Delft Center for Systems and Control, supervised by Gabriel de Albuquerque Gleizer. The research will allow you to gain deep insights across nonlinear dynamics, optimization, and theoretical computer science, and to combine those in new innovative ways. The position will offer you the opportunity to work on important problems with real-world impact and a strong publication potential. As the project progresses, you will also have the freedom to contribute to an experimental demonstration using a wireless lab-scale control system. Still, this position is theory-centric: expected outcomes include theoretical results, mathematical proofs, and computational algorithms, as well as open-source software and validation through simulations and analysis. Experimental demonstration is an option if it interests you.

Teaching activities are part of your PhD trajectory and may include, for example: supervising workgroups or lab sessions, assisting in courses, or mentoring BSc and MSc students. While teaching will not be your main responsibility, it offers valuable experience that supports your development and prepares you for future academic or professional roles. jobs.title: PhD in Spatiotemporal Light Generation with Frequency-Gradient Metasurfaces
jobs.description_html:
How can we control light in space, time, and frequency to make photonic systems faster, more compact, and more versatile?
In this PhD project, you will develop frequency-gradient metasurfaces for ultrafast beam steering, temporal focusing, and self-torque, combining design, nanofabrication, and femtosecond experiments.

Information
Current photonic components can shape light with remarkable spatial precision, but controlling its spatial, spectral, and temporal structure simultaneously remains far more difficult. This limits how fast, compact, and versatile optical systems can become. In this PhD project, you will develop frequency-gradient metasurfaces that couple these degrees of freedom and enable ultrafast control of structured light. The aim is to realize beam steering, temporal focusing, and self-torque generation on femtosecond timescales, and to establish compact platforms relevant to next-generation imaging, communication, and photonic information processing.

Your research will span the full cycle from concept to experiment. You will:
  • Develop design strategies for 2D and 3D frequency-gradient metasurfaces.
  • Model and optimize their electromagnetic, spectral, and dispersive response.
  • Explore ultrafast beam steering, temporal focusing, and self-torque generation through harmonic beating.
  • Fabricate the designed nanophotonic structures using TU/e cleanroom facilities.
  • Build femtosecond optical experiments to characterize the generated spatiotemporal light fields.
  • Use experimental results to refine the designs and improve device performance.

The project is part of SPARK – Spatiotemporal Photonic Technologies, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together academic and industrial partners across Europe. SPARK will train 15 doctoral candidates working across spatiotemporal metamaterials, structured light, ultrafast optics, nanophotonics, and advanced fabrication.

You will be based at Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) and supervised by Dr. Ahmed H. Dorrah, with Prof. Marco Piccardo at INESC MN, Portugal, as co-supervisor. A key part of the PhD is international and intersectoral training. You will spend 6 months at INESC MN in Portugal, focusing on theoretical modelling, holography, and ultrafast characterization, and 3 months at NKT Photonics in Denmark, working on supercontinuum-laser characterization.

You will also take part in SPARK training schools, workshops, webinars, conferences, and network-wide activities. These will give you exposure to different research environments, broaden your technical background, and connect you with researchers and industry partners across Europe.

At TU/e, you will join the Photonics and Semiconductor Nanophysics (PSN) group, where you will work in an interdisciplinary environment with strong expertise in nanophotonics, meta-optics, structured light, and optical characterization, with access to advanced nanofabrication and ultrafast optical facilities.

jobs.title: PhD in Dynamic Space–Time Interfaces for High-Speed THz Beam Control
jobs.description_html:
What new physics emerges when a THz interface changes on the timescale of the wave itself?
In this PhD project, you will develop dynamically modulated THz interfaces and explore frequency conversion, beam steering, and nonreciprocal propagation through electromagnetic design, device development, and THz experiments.

Information
The sub-THz regime is emerging as an important platform for future wireless communication, radar, and sensing, but controlling these waves dynamically remains a major challenge. Current interfaces can shape a THz wave in space, or tune their response in time, but doing both rapidly and with subwavelength spatial control is much harder. This limits how quickly THz beams can be steered, reconfigured, or made nonreciprocal.

In this PhD project, you will explore a different regime: space–time interfaces whose electromagnetic response changes while the wave is interacting with them. Fast modulation allows the interface to exchange energy and momentum with the field, enabling effects such as frequency conversion, dynamic beam steering, anomalous scattering, and nonreciprocal propagation.

Your research will span the full cycle from concept to experiment. You will:
  • Develop concepts for fast spatial and temporal modulation of THz waves.
  • Model wave interactions with dynamically changing interfaces.
  • Design structures combining subwavelength spatial control with high modulation rates.
  • Explore suitable modulation mechanisms, including MEMS-based architectures and alternative dynamic platforms.
  • Fabricate and experimentally characterize the resulting devices.
  • Build THz experiments to study beam steering, frequency shifts, and nonreciprocal response.
  • Demonstrate GHz-rate two-dimensional spatiotemporal beamforming and explore its use in reconfigurable and nonreciprocal THz communication.

The project will primarily target the sub-THz regime, approximately 0.3–1 THz. MEMS-based structures are one promising route, but the broader goal is to identify and realize practical platforms that can modulate THz waves fast enough to access genuinely dynamic wave phenomena.

The project is part of SPARK – Spatiotemporal Photonic Technologies, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together academic and industrial partners across Europe. You will be based at Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) and supervised by Dr. Ahmed H. Dorrah, with Prof. Michaël Lobet at Université de Namur, Belgium, as co-supervisor.

At TU/e, you will join the Photonics and Semiconductor Nanophysics (PSN) group, working in an interdisciplinary environment spanning photonics, electromagnetics, structured waves, nanofabrication, and experimental optics.

You will spend 6 months at Université de Namur, focusing on theoretical modelling of GHz space–time interfaces, and 3 months at TNO, working on THz mode (de)multiplexing and system-level characterization. You will also take part in SPARK training schools, workshops, conferences, and network-wide activities.

jobs.title: PhD Position Adaptive Optimization and Control of Offshore Energy Systems
jobs.description_html:
Job description
The Netherlands targets using only sustainable energy by 2050, yet 161 offshore oil and gas facilities are still active. Integrating renewables into their daily operation during phase-out can reduce environmental impact but introduces additional uncertainty, requiring costly and time-consuming implementation of new controllers as existing infrastructure is already equipped with functioning control structures. The central question now is: How can we enable practical implementation of optimization-based control in offshore energy systems with integrated renewables by building on existing control infrastructure?

Control systems in energy-intensive industries are designed to meet three goals: satisfy demand, ensure quality, and maintain safety. The ability to meet the goals combined with simplicity of implementation have been decisive factors when developing classic control systems, with environmental impact treated as an afterthought. Data-based controllers use advanced optimization algorithms to achieve these goals and meet environmental constraints. However, the complex mathematics involved makes them far from straightforward to implement in real-world infrastructure. This project aims to propose new adaptation methods for operating offshore facilities by merging online data-driven modelling to capture degradation of equipment over time with optimization-based methods to facilitate the transition to energy neutrality.

jobs.title: PhD Position on Twin Transition of Infrastructure: Paradoxical Leadership
jobs.description_html:
How do leaders make responsible decisions when digitalisation and sustainability goals pull in opposite directions? This PhD studies strategies on how infrastructure leaders navigate these tensions.

Job description
Digitalisation and sustainability are both transforming infrastructure, but they do not always align. Digital twins, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and other data-driven solutions can support better services and more sustainable operations, yet they can also create extra energy use and new dependencies. This PhD project asks how leaders in infrastructure organisations understand and navigate these tensions in their strategic and day-to-day decision-making.

This PhD post on paradoxical leadership is part of the NWO-funded Vidi "Infra-PaX" project. You will study how leaders and their teams (at a micro-level) deal with competing demands such as short-term performance versus long-term value and digital efficiency versus environmental impact. Rather than looking for simple “best practices”, the project examines how leaders work through persistent paradoxical tensions over time and how their responses evolve as the context changes. Please see more about the research here: https://youtu.be/bHaZjh5OXTQ

The research is designed as a longitudinal, embedded case study in the Dutch infrastructure domain. Your work will combine qualitative interviews, observations, document analysis and ethnographic fieldwork. The project will contribute to academic debates on paradox theory, leadership, infrastructure and project management. It will also generate practical outputs for the sector. Alongside your PhD thesis, you will be encouraged to publish in journals, present at conferences and take part in stakeholder-focused activities such as workshops, focus groups and knowledge-sharing events.

jobs.title: PhD Position on Twin Transition of Infrastructure: Ecosystem Orchestration
jobs.description_html:
How can public and private infrastructure actors align digitalisation and sustainability goals? This PhD studies how infrastructure projects can be organised amid long-term, interdependent pressures.

Job description
Infrastructure organisations do not navigate the twin transition alone. Digitalisation and sustainability are shaped across wider ecosystems that include owners, contractors, consultants, policymakers, regulators, suppliers and communities. These actors often depend on one another, but they do not always move at the same speed or work towards the same priorities. This PhD project investigates how such ecosystems can be orchestrated when digital and sustainability ambitions are interdependent, long-term and often contradictory.

This post on ecosystem orchestration is part of the NWO-funded Vidi "Infra-PaX" project. You will study how paradoxes in the twin transition emerge and can be navigated across public-private infrastructure ecosystems rather than within a single organisation (macro-level perspective). You will study issues such as top-down versus bottom-up change, tensions between short-term gains and long-term values and stakeholder alignment in projects. Please see more information about the research here: https://youtu.be/bHaZjh5OXTQ

The research is designed as an embedded case study in Dutch infrastructure. You will carry out interviews across the infrastructure ecosystem, analyse documents and strategies, and use systems thinking to map paradoxical tensions and their path-dependencies over time. Your work will contribute to research on infrastructure governance, inter-organisational collaboration, paradox theory and socio-technical transitions. You will produce tangible outputs that stakeholders can use directly. As part of the project, you will engage with practitioners and policymakers through collaborative activities.

You will be based at TU Delft and work in a multidisciplinary research environment connected to infrastructure management, project studies and sustainability transitions. The supervision will be by the project lead together with a broader interdisciplinary supervisory team of the section Integral Design & Management and strong links to industry and academic partners. jobs.title: PhD position in Systems and Control Theory for Energy-based Learning
jobs.description_html:
Are you excited about developing new mathematical foundations for energy-efficient computing? Do you want to contribute to cutting-edge research at the intersection of systems and control theory, optimization, circuit theory, and neuromorphic computing?

The University of Groningen is seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to work on a fundamental research project on systems and control theory for learning in neuromorphic circuits. Neuromorphic computing is an analog, brain-inspired computing paradigm with the potential to drastically reduce energy consumption while enabling faster inference than conventional digital architectures. A major challenge, however, is the development and analysis of dedicated algorithms for training analog circuits directly from data.


In this PhD project, you will develop a novel system-theoretic framework for learning in analog circuits and dissipative networks. We will view learning as a feedback interconnection of continuous-time (circuit) dynamics and an optimization algorithm. The key idea is to develop algorithms that minimise cost functions inspired by notions of energy, leading to highly efficient, local learning rules. 

What are you going to do?

As a PhD candidate, you will develop mathematical theory for learning in nonlinear and dynamic circuits. Building on preliminary results for resistive circuits, you will study circuits containing memristive and capacitive elements, as well as more general dissipative networks. The project combines systems and control theory, circuit theory, optimization, and machine learning, with the ultimate goal of advancing the mathematical foundations of physics-based learning.

Your responsibilities include:

  • Developing a system-theoretic framework that models learning as the feedback interconnection between continuous-time circuit dynamics and optimization algorithms.
  • Designing novel energy-based learning algorithms for training analog circuits directly from input-output data.
  • Developing fully decentralised learning rules that rely on local circuit information and are suitable for large-scale systems.
  • Establishing rigorous theoretical guarantees for convergence and scalability of the proposed learning algorithms.
  • Extending the theory from analog circuits to more general dissipative networks.
  • Testing and validating the developed methods.
  • Publishing research findings in leading international journals and conferences and presenting your work at scientific meetings.
  • Contributing to teaching activities and supervising Bachelor's and Master's students where appropriate.

jobs.title: PhD in Contrast Ultrasound Imaging of Nanobubbles for Cancer Diagnostics
jobs.description_html:
Want to help replace painful prostate biopsies with smarter ultrasound? Join MOMENTUM, an NWO-funded project developing nanobubble-enhanced ultrasound imaging for cancer diagnostics, and design the pharmacokinetic models and signal analysis methods that turn nanobubble transport into a diagnostic biomarker.

Information
Prostate cancer is the most common cancer among men in the Netherlands, and its diagnosis still relies heavily on invasive biopsies. More accurate, noninvasive ultrasound imaging could reduce this burden considerably, but current contrast agents cannot fully capture the abnormal blood vessels that feed a tumor. Nanobubbles, a new generation of ultrasound contrast agent far smaller than those used today, promise to change that by reaching into the tumor tissue itself.

We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate to develop the modeling and signal analysis methods that turn nanobubble ultrasound imaging into a quantitative diagnostic tool. You will work with imaging data acquired from lab-grown vascular models and translate the changes they show over time into pharmacokinetic and spatiotemporal models that describe how nanobubbles move through and beyond the microvasculature. The resulting parameters are candidate biomarkers for tumor angiogenesis, with prostate cancer as the initial clinical focus.

This PhD position is part of MOMENTUM, a project funded by the NWO Open Technology Programme that combines microfluidics, bubble physics, and ultrasound signal processing to bring nanobubble imaging closer to clinical use. You will collaborate closely with a fellow PhD candidate, a postdoc, and a technician working on the other parts of the project at TU/e and the University of Twente, as well as with industrial and clinical partners including Bracco, Angiogenesis Analytics, and the Amsterdam UMC. This position will be embedded in the Biomedical Diagnostics (BM/d) lab (Signal Processing Systems group, Department of Electrical Engineering, TU/e), and you will be supervised daily by dr. Simona Turco (s.turco@tue.nl), together with prof. Massimo Mischi.

jobs.title: PhD in Dynamic Metasurfaces for Spacetime-Engineered Light
jobs.description_html:
Are you fascinated by the idea of steering light through time as well as space? Develop metasurfaces for synthetic crystal rotation and nonreciprocal light-matter interactions, with secondments at UPNA, Spain and UltraFast Innovations GmbH, Germany.

Information
We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate with a background in photonics, optics, or applied physics to contribute to SPARK Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral network. The candidate will develop metasurfaces supporting synthetic crystal rotation through ultrafast spatiotemporal modulation. The project involves theoretical modelling and simulation of anisotropic metasurfaces with epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) like behaviour, realization of dynamically modulated metasurface structures, and experimental evaluation of their ultrafast optical response, with the aim of demonstrating synthetic spacetime rotation, generating spatiotemporal light fields, and uncovering nonreciprocal light–matter interactions.

The PhD candidate will work within the Photonic Integration group at the Department of Electrical Engineering, Eindhoven University of Technology, co-supervised by Prof. I. Liberal at the University of Navarra (UPNA), Spain, The candidate will be part of a multidisciplinary, international team within the SPARK MSCA Doctoral network, working alongside PhD students and researchers on related nonreciprocal and spatiotemporal photonics technologies, with close collaboration across theory, fabrication, and experimental characterization.

The research and secondment activities will be supported by a 6-month stay at the University of Navarra (UPNA), Spain, focused on theoretical modelling, and a 3-month stay at UFI for ultrafast optical characterization, giving the candidate direct access to complementary expertise and facilities across the consortium.

jobs.title: PhD in Spatiotemporal Integrated Metamaterials
jobs.description_html:
Are you fascinated by nonreciprocal photonics? Design dynamically modulated, on-chip metamaterials for nonreciprocal light control, with secondments at INESC MN and PICadvanced, Portugal.

Information
We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate with a background in photonics, optics, or nanofabrication to contribute to SPARK Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral network. The candidate will develop chip-scale metamaterials with time-varying modulation for nonreciprocal photonic devices. The project involves theoretical and numerical design of dynamically modulated structures, on-chip fabrication using advanced nanolithography, and experimental demonstration of nonreciprocal light transport, with the aim of realizing dynamically modulated metamaterials for nonreciprocal light control and integrating them into photonic circuits for optical communication and quantum applications.

The PhD candidate will work within the Photonic Integration group at the Department of Electrical Engineering, Eindhoven University of Technology, co-supervised by Prof. M. Piccardo at INESC MN, Portugal. The candidate will be part of a multidisciplinary, international team within the SPARK MSCA Doctoral network, working alongside PhD students and researchers on related nonreciprocal and photonic integration technologies, with close collaboration across design, fabrication, and characterization.

The research and secondment activities will be supported by a 6-month stay at INESC MN, Portugal, focused on component measurements, and a 3-month stay at PICadvanced for chip-level integration, giving the candidate direct access to complementary expertise and facilities across the consortium.

jobs.title: PhD position on local food web dynamics within offshore wind farms
jobs.description_html:
PhD position on local food web dynamics within offshore wind farms in the North Sea POWER (Progress in Offshore Wind Ecological Research) consortium.

As offshore wind farms rapidly expand in the North Sea, mitigating their ecological impact on marine ecosystems is critical. The North Sea POWER project addresses this challenge by filling vital knowledge gaps regarding underwater noise, biomass and water flows, and wildlife disturbance (such as seabirds and bats) to support a sustainable green energy transition. By reducing uncertainty in models and identifying effective mitigation options, North Sea POWER supports offshore wind development that protects marine ecosystems while contributing to a sustainable energy future.

The project is funded through the Dutch Research Agenda (NWA), developed in collaboration with the Dutch Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy.

Led by Wageningen University & Research, the project brings together a transdisciplinary consortium of leading academic institutions, societal stakeholders, conservation organisations, and energy sector partners. More about the consortium.

This position is one of twelve PhD and postdoc positions across the consortium. You will be part of a team working on shared questions, with joint meetings, fieldwork and training alongside your own project. You will be hosted at Wageningen Marine Research in Den Helder, where you will study how fouling communities in offshore wind farms affect local food web dynamics and carbon cycling in close collaboration with Wageningen University. Part of the molecular lab work will be performed in the lab of Marine Animal Ecology in Wageningen.

Are you interested in how biofouling communities in offshore wind farms affect local food web dynamics and carbon cycling?
We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate to join our research team on biofouling with a focus on quantifying how biofouling communities influence primary and secondary production and blue carbon sequestration in the seabed. By combining laboratory experiments, in-situ fieldwork observations, and ecosystem modelling, your work will help refine current ecosystem-scale models and inform environmental impact assessments.

Your duties and responsibilities include:
  • conduct laboratory experiments to measure and quantify grazing rates, carbon biomass, prey preferences, particle export, and faeces sinking velocity rates across different fouling species;
  • execute field surveys from research vessels;
  • integrate empirical data into conceptual models;
  • publish research findings in peer-reviewed journals and present them at national and international conferences;
  • mentor BSc/MSc students.

Your team
You will be part of Wageningen Marine Research (WMR – Den Helder), as a member of the Theme Team North Sea Reefs with Dr. Joop Coolen, and Dr. Ninon Mavraki as your daily supervisors, and you are also part of the Marine Animal Ecology Group (MAE) supervised by the Associate Professor Reindert Nijland at Wageningen University and Research. In Den Helder a broad group of scientists, analysts, field workers and students work on a variety of topics, such as benthic ecology, seals, seabirds, bats and other species. You will be a member of the theme team North Sea Reefs, with multiple colleagues specialising in the ecology of natural and artificial reefs in the North Sea. Furthermore, you will have the opportunity to design experiments involving molecular tools, such as eDNA and DNA metabarcoding, which then will be performed at the molecular laboratory of MAE in Wageningen University.

You will work here
The position is available within Wageningen University & Research at the Marine Animal Ecology group. The organisation has good and flexible employment conditions, including good education and training facilities for PhD students. Your working location will be at Wageningen Marine Research in Den Helder, the Netherlands, where the daily supervisors Joop Coolen and Ninon Mavraki are located. WMR is an applied research institute with 3 locations (Den Helder, IJmuiden and Yerseke) in the Netherlands. Research areas in Den Helder include coastal and offshore North Sea, tropics and (ant)arctic regions. In addition to ecological research, WMR advises the government regarding protection of species and habitats, pollution, and other anthropogenic interactions with ecology, and collaborate with industry, i.a. to study nature inclusive designs. Facilities in Den Helder in addition to offices, include a benthic lab, eco-analysis lab, climate rooms, mesocosms and algae culture facilities. Additionally, WMR has an experimental hard substrate garden in the marina on the island of Texel.

jobs.title: Promovendus arts-onderzoeker Anesthesiologie & Gynaecologische Oncologie
jobs.description_html:
Wil jij onderzoeken hoe we het herstel van vrouwen na een grote operatie voor gynaecologische kanker kunnen verbeteren? En wil je werken op het snijvlak van anesthesiologie, gynaecologische oncologische chirurgie en perioperatieve zorg?

Binnen het UMCG starten we een grote, landelijk uitgevoerde gerandomiseerde studie naar pijnbehandeling en herstel na open chirurgie voor gynaecologische kanker. Voor deze studie zoeken de afdelingen Anesthesiologie en Gynaecologische Oncologie gezamenlijk een enthousiaste promovendus/(arts-)onderzoeker.

Wat ga jij doen
Als promovendus krijg je een centrale rol in de uitvoering en coördinatie van de studie. Je werkt vanuit het UMCG nauw samen met onderzoekers en zorgprofessionals binnen de Anesthesiologie en Gynaecologische Oncologie en met de deelnemende centra Amsterdam UMC en Catharina Ziekenhuis Eindhoven.
Je houdt je onder andere bezig met:
- het verder uitwerken en operationaliseren van het onderzoeksprotocol;
- het voorbereiden van de studie en de indiening bij de METC;
- coördinatie van de multicenter studie;
- screening, inclusie en follow-up van patiënten;
- bewaken van inclusie, datakwaliteit en protocol adherence;
- analyseren en interpreteren van de onderzoeksgegevens;
- uitvoeren van deelstudies rondom patiëntgerapporteerde uitkomsten, implementatie en kosteneffectiviteit;
- presenteren van resultaten op nationale en internationale congressen;
- schrijven van wetenschappelijke publicaties en een proefschrift.
Het patiëntenperspectief staat in deze studie centraal. Patiëntvertegenwoordigers van Stichting Olijf en de UMCG Cliëntenraad zijn vanaf de ontwikkeling van het onderzoek betrokken en blijven gedurende de studie participeren.

jobs.title: PhD Position: Curiosity in the Classroom
jobs.description_html:
Are you fascinated by how curiosity shapes learning in the classroom? Would you like to investigate how children seek information, explore and learn in real-world educational settings? If so, then we invite you to apply for this PhD position on Curiosity in the Classroom at Radboud University.

Curiosity is a powerful driver of learning, yet we still know relatively little about how curiosity unfolds in the classroom and how educational environments can support children in becoming curious and actively seeking information. In this PhD project, you will investigate curiosity in 10-to 12-year-old children within authentic educational settings.

The project combines experimental research, classroom studies and computational modelling to better understand what makes children curious, how they decide which information to explore, and how different ways of structuring learning environments influence curiosity and learning. Computational models will be used to characterise individual differences in information-seeking behaviour and to examine how these differences relate to learning in the classroom. A central aim is to translate insights from fundamental research on curiosity into educational practice.

You will design and conduct studies in collaboration with primary schools and educational partners, review the scientific literature, recruit and test participants, develop and evaluate educational materials and experimental tasks, analyse behavioural data, apply computational modelling techniques, and write scientific articles that will form the basis of your dissertation.

You will work closely with your supervisors, another PhD candidate investigating the cognitive neuroscience of curiosity, and a broader interdisciplinary team of researchers in psychology, cognitive neuroscience and educational science. You will also collaborate with schools, teachers and educational organisations to conduct research in real-world learning environments.

The position involves frequent communication with children, parents, teachers, schools and other stakeholders, presenting your work to national and international audiences, and contributing to teaching for approximately 10% of your time.

Would you like to learn more about what it’s like to pursue a PhD at Radboud University? Visit the page about working as a PhD candidate.

jobs.title: PhD: Analysing and Mapping strontium and zinc in cremations (AMASZINC)
jobs.description_html:
Starting date: March 1, 2027

We offer a four-year PhD position within the NWO-funded AMASZINC (Analysing and MApping Strontium and Zinc IN Cremations to reconstruct diet, mobility, and funerary practices of ancient human and animal populations) project, which aims to develop new ways of studying mobility, diet, and funerary practices from cremated human and animal remains. The project combines cutting-edge laser ablation techniques with Sr and Zn concentration and isotope ratio analysis to unlock information preserved in burnt bone. The project is carried out in close collaboration with Prof. Christophe Snoeck at Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) and Dr. Klervia Jaouen at Observatoire Midi Pyrénées/CNRS, Toulouse, France, offering opportunities to work across institutions and research fields.

Your duties
  • investigating mobility and dietary histories as well as funerary practices of Iron Age and Roman populations from the Netherlands, Belgium, Slovenia, and Portugal
  • performing laser ablation mapping of cremated bone
  • conducting high-precision ⁸⁷Sr/⁸⁶Sr and δ⁸⁸Sr analyses using TIMS and MC-ICP-MS
  • developing and testing new approaches for Zn concentrations and isotope ratio analysis of cremated bone

jobs.title: PhD-TA in Statistics
jobs.description_html:
Are you our next PhD candidate in functional data analysis? Are you passionate about developing statistical methodology for complex, dynamic data? Join our team to develop methods for estimating time-varying network structures and detecting structural changes in functional time series.

Information
In many scientific fields, observations are increasingly collected in the form of functions rather than simple numerical measurements. Examples include brain signals recorded continuously over time, and economic indicators observed as curves or distributions. Such functional time series often exhibit temporal dependence, non-stationarity, and complex non-Euclidean structures. These features contain valuable information, but they also make conventional statistical methods difficult to apply and can lead to unreliable conclusions.

Network structures provide a useful way to describe the relationships among the components of these complex data. In neuroscience, for example, connections between brain regions may be inferred from functional imaging signals rather than observed directly. Understanding which connections are present, how they evolve over time, and when structural changes occur is essential for scientific interpretation. Existing methods may produce false or missed connections when the observations are dependent, non-stationary, and non-Euclidean.

In this project, you will investigate theoretical tools for analysing dependence structures in functional time series. You will develop new methods and statistical softwares for constructing time-varying networks, detecting structural changes, and controlling false connections in complex settings. The proposed methods will contribute to deeper insights in distinguishing connections and changes from random variation in scientific studies. The PhD candidate will be supervised by Lujia Bai and Jeanine Duistermaat, and will publish in international scientific journals, participate in international conferences, and develop an independent research profile.

You will join the Statistics, Probability and Operations Research (SPOR) cluster in the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science at Eindhoven University of Technology. The cluster offers a collaborative research environment that connects time series analysis, functional data and network analysis. We work closely with external partners who drive innovation and growth, and our research is strongly embedded in applications such as anomaly detection, process monitoring and improvement, weather and climate forecasting, and statistical bioinformatics.

As an ideal candidate, you have a strong affinity for mathematical statistics and rigorous proofs, as well as a passion for developing and implementing novel methods and applying them to real-world data.

jobs.title: PhD in Control Theory for Learned Operators in Dynamical Systems
jobs.description_html:
Are you fascinated by the intersection of control theory and scientific machine learning? Join us in developing the mathematical foundations needed to make deep operators reliable, robust, and applicable for control of complex engineering systems. In this PhD project, you will investigate how operator-learning models can represent dynamical systems, how their stability and robustness can be characterized, and how controllers can be designed for them. Your work will combine rigorous theory, numerical methods, and applications in high-tech, medical, and energy systems.

Information
Modern engineering increasingly relies on data-driven models to describe complex dynamical systems. Scientific machine learning is now enabling a new class of models that learn operators mapping system inputs and initial conditions directly to system responses. These learned operators offer exciting opportunities for efficient simulation, digital twins, optimization, and control.

In this PhD project, you will develop a new systems and control theory for learned operators, bridging modern scientific machine learning with classical control theory. Rather than focusing on a single machine-learning architecture, you will establish mathematical principles that apply across a broad class of operator-learning methods, including current and future deep operator models.

Your research will investigate fundamental questions such as: when does a learned operator admit an equivalent state-space representation? How can stability, contraction, dissipativity, robustness, and other system-theoretic properties be defined and guaranteed directly in the operator domain? And how can feedforward, feedback, and predictive controllers be designed for systems represented by learned operators? You will combine analytical theory with numerical implementation and validate the developed methods on industrially relevant applications in the high-tech, medical, and energy sectors.

You will become part of the Dynamics and Control group at the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology, under the supervision of dr.ir. Fahim Shakib and prof.dr.ir. Nathan van de Wouw. You will contribute to research at the intersection of systems and control theory, scientific machine learning, operator theory, optimization, and applied mathematics. You will work in an interdisciplinary environment with opportunities to collaborate with academic and industrial partners. You will be part of a vibrant and socially interactive group of approximately 35 researchers in the field of dynamical systems and control.

jobs.title: PhD Position on How Vegetation Influences Soil Microbial Processes and Carbon Cycling Across Scales
jobs.description_html:
How does vegetation protect soil microorganisms from climate extremes, and what does this mean for ecosystem carbon cycling? Climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of droughts and heat waves, impacting ecosystem carbon storage worldwide. Join the Institute for Biodiversity and Ecosystem Dynamics (IBED) in this interdisciplinary project to uncover how vegetation traits and structure shape below-ground microclimates, which in turn regulate soil microbial processes and influence ecosystem carbon cycling across.

About the position
Climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of droughts, with profound consequences for ecosystem carbon cycling. While drought effects on aboveground vegetation have been studied extensively, our understanding of how vegetation structure and functional traits influence belowground microbial processes and carbon stocks remains limited. Soils store more carbon than the atmosphere and vegetation combined, so even small changes belowground can have major implications for carbon storage and climate feedbacks.

Vegetation strongly modifies the microclimate experienced by soils. By reducing radiation and evaporative demand from the soil surface, plants moderate extremes in soil temperature and moisture while simultaneously altering carbon allocation belowground. These changes can influence microbial activity, community composition and carbon cycling, potentially buffering ecosystems against drought and heat waves. However, the magnitude of these effects, the mechanisms involved, and their consequences across ecosystem components remain poorly understood. The combined observation of soil processes with plant functional traits and structure of vegetation captured by remote sensing (e.g. LiDAR, multi- and hyper-spectral imagery) in experiments and at contrasting field-sites provide us insights on how soil microbial composition and diversity responds to a shift of vegetation types, climate, and land cover.

In this PhD project, you will investigate how vegetation traits and structure regulate below-ground microclimate and microbial carbon cycling across spatial scales. You will combine controlled experiments, field observations, remote sensing data, ecosystem flux measurements and process-based modelling to identify the mechanisms linking vegetation, soil microorganisms and ecosystem carbon cycling. The project spans laboratory, field and ecosystem scales and combines measurements ranging from microbial processes to ecosystem carbon fluxes.

You will be jointly supervised by Dr. Yifang Shi, Dr. Albert C. Brangarí, Dr. Emiel van Loon, and Prof. Franciska de Vries, whose complementary expertise in vegetation structure and functional traits, ecosystem carbon cycling, soil microbial ecology, remote sensing and process-based modelling provides a unique interdisciplinary training environment. The project will also include a postdoctoral researcher. As part of this team, you will collaborate with national and international partners, including the Integrated Carbon Observation System (ICOS), and become part of a vibrant research environment.

What are you going to do?
As a PhD candidate, you will develop an interdisciplinary research programme together with a postdoc researcher, combining experiments, field observations and modelling to understand how vegetation regulates soil microbial responses to drought and heat, and the implications for carbon.

Tasks and responsibilities:
  • performing laboratory experiments and field campaigns at the ICOS ecosystem station Loobos and other sites;
  • quantifying soil microclimate, microbial activity, community composition and carbon cycling;
  • assessing vegetation structure and functional traits using remote sensing techniques (e.g. multi- and hyper-spectral imagery, LiDAR);
  • analyzing chamber and eddy covariance measurements;
  • applying process-based models to integrate observations across biological and spatial scales;
  • publishing your findings in international peer-reviewed journals;
  • presenting your research at national and international conferences;
  • contributing to teaching and supervising Bachelor's and Master’s students.

Your profile
We are looking for an enthusiastic and ambitious candidate with a strong interest in vegetation structure and functioning, soil microbial ecology and ecosystem carbon cycling, and an interest in the challenge of combining experiments, remote sensing and modelling to answer fundamental ecological questions.

Your experience and profile:
  • an MSc degree in the Natural Sciences (e.g. Earth Science, Biology, Ecology, Physics) or Engineering;

Additional qualifications that would be an advantage include experience with:
  • remote sensing data analysis (e.g. multi- and hyper-spectral imagery, LiDAR);
  • process-based carbon modelling;
  • plant functional traits;
  • eddy-covariance and other carbon flux measurements;
  • soil microbial ecology and biogeochemistry.

jobs.title: PhD Agrochemical impacts on microbial carbon cycling in aquatic ecosystems
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in the impacts of agricultural land use on microbial communities? Do you want to understand the effects of pesticides and nutrients on carbon cycling in aquatic ecosystems? The Institute of Biodiversity and Ecosystem Dynamics is looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to investigate agrochemical impacts on microbial carbon cycling in lowland agricultural drainage ditch sediments.

About the position
Agricultural land use strongly alters the functioning and biodiversity of the surrounding landscape. Conventional practices rely heavily on chemical inputs, such as fertilizers and pesticides, which readily make their way into adjacent waterways. Yet how these agrochemicals affect aquatic microbial communities and their functioning remains poorly understood. This is a pressing research priority, since the Netherlands has approximately 300,000 km of drainage ditches. These ditches hold huge ecological potential, supporting ecosystem services such as carbon cycling and water transport, but they are also most heavily exposed to agrochemical inputs — a combination that may threaten biodiversity and undermine the very services they provide.

This PhD position will focus on aquatic microbial ecotoxicology, aiming to unravel the effects of agrochemicals on the structure and functioning of microbial and viral communities in agricultural ditch sediments and the linked ecosystem function of carbon cycling. It incorporates pesticide mixture toxicity, which is severely understudied, especially to viruses, bacteria, archaea, and fungi. As such, it goes beyond the effects of single chemicals on single organisms and takes a wide scope of microbial diversity and a key ecosystem function – carbon cycling, including both sediment carbon pools and greenhouse gas emissions. This project will broaden our understanding of the impacts of agrochemicals from being toxic to aquatic life to the intertwined consequences for global warming.

The position will be based at the Institute for Biodiversity and Ecosystem Dynamics (IBED) of the University of Amsterdam, bridging the Departments of Freshwater and Marine Ecology (FAME) and Ecosystem and Landscape Dynamics (ELD).

What are you going to do?
You will address this multidisciplinary topic using state-of-the-art analytical techniques and data processing and analysis, guided by the highly qualified support staff at IBED. Together with your supervisors, you will bridge the fields of aquatic ecotoxicology, environmental chemistry, and microbial ecology. This requires thinking outside the traditional spheres of these fields, and demands creativity and flexibility as well as a strong motivation to address this challenge using multiple lines of evidence.

jobs.title: PhD Candidate in Ecological Modelling of Krill and Salps in a Changing Southern Ocean
jobs.description_html:
Are you excited by ecosystem modeling, climate change and polar oceans? Do you enjoy quantitative work, coding, and turning ecology into equations? We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate who is eager to study Antarctic krill and salp population dynamics, and their impacts on Southern Ocean carbon export in a changing climate.

About the position
The Southern Ocean plays a disproportionately large role in the global ocean carbon cycle. Its carbon cycling is strongly influenced by zooplankton, especially Antarctic krill and salps, whose fecal pellets drive vertical carbon export. Krill depend closely on sea ice and under‑ice habitats, while salps thrive in warmer, often ice‑free waters. Warming and sea‑ice loss are already shifting their distributions and increasing spatial overlap, with implications for competition, food webs, and fisheries. Yet current ecosystem models represent these key grazers only crudely, leaving major uncertainties in future projections.

This project asks how changing interactions between Antarctic krill and salps reshape Southern Ocean ecosystems and the global carbon cycle. It will explore how sea‑ice loss, warming, predation and fisheries affect krill and salp population dynamics, and how shifts in their relative dominance alter grazing, fecal pellet production and vertical carbon export. Ultimately, it aims to reduce uncertainty in projections of Southern Ocean functioning under future climate and fishing scenarios.

What are you going to do?
You will develop stage‑structured population models for both species, explicitly including life‑history processes, sea‑ice dependence, predation and fisheries. You will couple these models to an ocean-sea‑ice-biogeochemical framework for the Antarctic Peninsula to quantify impacts on vertical carbon export. Finally, you will explore future climate and fishing scenarios to assess how shifts in krill-salp dominance affect Southern Ocean functioning.

Tasks and responsibilities:
  • Complete and defend a PhD thesis within the official appointment duration of four years
  • Develop and analyze stage-structured population models for krill and salp
  • Couple the stage-structured models to an ocean-sea ice-biogeochemical framework to quantify how zooplankton life-histories influences vertical carbon export and local carbon cycling
  • Publish your results in international scientific journals
  • Present your results at meetings and scientific conferences
  • Discuss your work in our group meetings, incorporate feedback, and give input to others
  • Assist in teaching activities and in supervising bachelor and master students

Your profile
Your experience and profile:
  • Completed, or soon-to-be completed MSc in the biological sciences or different fields in the natural sciences (e.g. computational, mathematical, earth or marine sciences) with a strong interest in ecology and modeling
  • Demonstrated experience with mathematical modelling, and an ability to learn new concepts and (computational) methods as needed
  • A demonstrated ability to work with programming languages such as R, Python, Matlab, or C++
  • A keen interest in advancing our understanding of marine ecosystems, polar regions, and/or biogeochemistry
  • Proficient communication skills in spoken and written English
  • Experience in scientific writing, bifurcation analysis or numerical ocean modeling are considered a plus.

Our offer
A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students. The preferred starting date is as soon as possible. For this position the University Job Classification profile “Promovendus” (PhD candidate) applies. Your salary will be € 3.204 gross per month in the first year and will increase to € 4.051 in the final year, based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week. In addition, you will receive a 8% holiday allowance and 8.3% year-end allowance.

A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants.

The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable.

Besides the salary and a vibrant and challenging environment at Science Park we offer you multiple fringe benefits:
  • 232 holiday hours per year (based on fulltime) and extra holidays between Christmas and 1 January;
  • multiple courses to follow from our Teaching and Learning Centre;
  • a complete educational program for PhD students;
  • multiple courses on topics such as leadership for academic staff;
  • multiple courses on topics such as time management, handling stress and an online learning platform with 100+ different courses;
  • 7 weeks birth leave (partner leave) with 100% salary;
  • partly paid parental leave;
  • the possibility to set up a workplace at home;
  • a pension at ABP for which UvA pays two third part of the contribution;
  • the possibility to follow courses to learn Dutch;
  • help with registration at UvA- Housing for a studio or small apartment when you’re moving from abroad.

Are you curious to read more about our extensive package of secondary employment benefits, take a look here.

About us
The Institute for Biodiversity and Ecosystem Dynamics (IBED) is one of eight research institutes of the Faculty of Science at the University of Amsterdam. The research at IBED aims to unravel how ecosystems function in all their complexity, and how they change due to natural processes and human activities. At its core lies an integrated systems approach to study biodiversity, ecosystems and the environment. IBED adopts this systems approach to ecosystems, addressing abiotic (soil and water quality) and biotic factors (ecology and evolution of plants, animals, and microorganisms), and the interplay between those. The IBED vision includes research encompassing experimental and theoretical approaches at a wide variety of temporal and spatial scales, i.e. from molecules and microorganisms to patterns and processes occurring at the global scale. The University of Amsterdam has excellent high performance computing facilities. Furthermore, IBED has a dedicated computational support team with specialized knowledge of bioinformatics, (geo)database management and scientific programming. IBED also works with non-academic partners to deliver transdisciplinary science for society.

The position will be based in the Department of Freshwater and Marine Ecology. The department of Freshwater & Marine Ecology aims to increase our understanding of the biodiversity and dynamics of freshwater and marine ecosystems from the level of molecules and genes to entire ecosystems.

Department of Theoretical and Computational Ecology. Research in the Department of Theoretical and Computational Ecology focuses on understanding the complexity of ecological systems by using theoretical and advanced computational approaches.

Want to know more about our organisation? Read more about working at the University of Amsterdam.

jobs.title: PhD Position (1 FTE) in the area of Belonging of European Muslims to the EU
jobs.description_html:
The Institute for History at the University of Leiden invites applications for:

PhD Position (1 FTE) in the area of Belonging of European Muslims to the EU
The PhD candidate will become part of the NOW Open-L funded project “European Muslims and Belonging to the EU, 2015-2025’ led by Professor Sarah Wolff. The expected starting date is 1 January 2027.

Project description
This project asks What is the sense of belonging of European Muslims to the European Union (EU)? How do they relate to the EU? And how do they experience their EU citizenship? Is there a relationship between sense of belonging, agency and representation in EU institutions? And how are EU and national institutions taking into account this minority in its policy-making? The main scientific objective is to answer these under-researched questions, and to deliver the first study of European Muslims’ belonging to the EU which will conceptualize how European Muslims experience, contest, embrace and negotiate their belonging to the EU. In this project, European Muslims are defined as people self-identifying as Muslims with EU citizenship. Belonging relates to emotional attachment, political values and ethical commitments to the EU as a political community. The project hypothesizes that belonging varies across three dimensions: institutional (how the EU frame belonging), transnational (social mobilisation) and societal (individuals).

Moving away from conventional studies on Muslims in Europe, as foreigners and immigrants, this project considers Muslims as Europeans and agents of their own belonging to the EU. The project has four main scientific objectives: (1) Analysing how the politics of belonging are produced by EU institutions and what space is given to ‘belonging’ and who can belong (2) To document and trace the ways European Muslims are active transnational and bottom-up agents through mobilisation, demonstrations and court litigation at EU level. (3) To use insights from Bulgaria, France and The Netherlands to theorize the varieties of belonging regimes of European Muslims and explain why this may vary across countries, communities and individuals. (4) To survey and examine what meaning do European Muslims give to belonging to the EU and what it means for the Future of Europe and European Democracy.

The candidate’s Profile
We are looking a candidate who will contribute primarily to WP2 ‘Agency of Belonging in Europe’ which addresses objective 2. The candidate will also contribute across the WPs and maybe more specifically to Objective 1. The successful candidate will investigate how European Muslims act as transnational and bottom-up agents, and how they actively shape, negotiate and contest their sense of belonging to European communities and institutions. Particular attention will be paid to mobilisation, demonstrations and strategic litigation at the national and EU levels, as well as to how these forms of political participation interact with and shape EU politics of belonging.

The research will draw on EU studies, social movement theory, digital methods and discourse analysis to examine transnational collective action among European Muslims. It will aim to understand how European Muslims actively shape, negotiate claim, contest their sense of belonging in a community such as the EU. The candidate will analyse selected pan-European organisations and networks, including Muslims and non-Muslims organisations such the Forum of European Muslim Youth and Student Organisation, the European Network Against Racism. A case selection of mobilisation campaigns and political issues—including anti-racism and anti-Islamophobia, freedom of religion or belief, EU foreign policy and climate change—will be conducted. The PhD student will have the opportunity to contribute to the various deliverables across the working packages. The candidate will also contribute to the project's broader analysis of how European Muslims participate in and transform European politics, thereby contributing to Objective 1 on the changing forms of agency, citizenship and belonging in Europe.

Key responsibilities
  • Completion of a PhD thesis within four years;
  • Participation in meetings of the project research group;
  • Presentations of intermediate research results at workshops and conferences;
  • Participation in the training programme of one of the Graduate Schools;
  • Co-organizing workshop and conference.
  • Contributing to public outputs such as podcasts or policy briefs.

Requirements for PhD candidate
  • An MA or RMES in political science, international relations, European (Union) studies, migration, or sociology held by time of appointment, with an MA thesis of high quality. If the degree is not yet obtained at the time of application, a statement by the applicant’s supervisor should confirm that it will be obtained by time of appointment;
  • Well-developed research skills including interview skills, mostly qualitative, but quantitative is a plus.
  • Ability to work both independently and as part of an (international) team;
  • Excellent command of English and ability to read and analyse Arabic-language written and digital sources. Knowledge of French, Dutch, Bulgarian, Turkish, Moroccan Arabic (Darija), or other languages relevant to Muslim communities in France, the Netherlands, Bulgaria, and across the EU is an advantage.
  • Good writing skills;
  • Interest in the European Union, Belonging, Minorities in Europe, Muslims.
  • The PhD candidate will be required to live and work from the Netherlands.

Information
For more information, contact professor Sarah Wolff, s.wolff@hum.leidenuniv.nl

About our organisation
Since its founding in 1575, Leiden University has acquired an international reputation for excellent teaching and research. With its staff of over 800, the Faculty of Humanities provides 26 Bachelors and 27 Masters programmes for over 7,200 students based at locations in Leiden and The Hague.

The Institute for History is the home of a vibrant community of researchers and lecturers with outstanding track records and successful in attracting national and international research grants.

Under the label ‘Global Questions, Local Sources’ scholars affiliated to the Institute combine a deep knowledge of global interactions and of specific localities, regions and states in Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas. They use comparative, connective and entangled approaches and resort to qualitative and quantitative research methodologies. For more information on the Institute for History: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/humanities/institute-for-history/phd-programme.

Diversity and Inclusion
Leiden University’s Institute for History embraces diversity and seeks candidates who will contribute to a climate that supports students and staff of all identities and backgrounds. We strongly encourage individuals from underrepresented and/or marginalized backgrounds to apply.

Terms and Conditions
We offer a full-time position for initially one year. After a positive evaluation of the progress of the thesis, personal capabilities and compatibility the appointment will be extended by a further three years. Salary range from € 3,204.- to € 4,051.- gross per month (pay scale P, in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities).

jobs.title: PhD candidate, Dutch morphology and constructicography
jobs.description_html:
Faculty of Humanities, Leiden University Centre for Linguistics

PhD candidate, Dutch morphology and constructicography
Starting date: January 2027 (a later starting date can be negotiated)

Deadline: November 1, 2026

Description
Leiden University Centre for Linguistics (LUCL) invites applications for a fully funded PhD position within the NWO project ‘The Morphicon: A new gateway to morphological knowledge’.

The PhD in this project will work in a small team to build a morphological constructicon for Dutch and use it to investigate the division of labour between grammatical regularity and lexical idiosyncrasy.

Constructicons are digital networks of grammatical constructions in a language. Such resources are being built for a variety of major languages, but not yet for Dutch. Moreover, existing constructicons all focus on syntactic constructions, neglecting morphology. The aim of this project is to develop the first morphological constructicon or “Morphicon” with Dutch as the target language. The resource will be developed by a team of three researchers—the PI, a Postdoc and the PhD—in collaboration with the Instituut voor de Nederlandse Taal.

The PhD will participate in the team effort, but will also have their own research project.

The team will work together on transforming existing lexicographic and grammatical resources into a digital network. The network will consist of lexical constructions (simple and complex words) and grammatical constructions (word-formation patterns), linked to one another by the properties they share. An important part of the work will be to find, test and develop digital tools to assist in classification, annotation and network building.

The specific research project of the PhD will target the interplay between grammatical regularity and lexical idiosyncrasy in morphological constructions. To this aim, the PhD will investigate a set of selected constructional families in greater depth to assess the proportion and nature of idiosyncrasy within each family.

This PhD position is part of an NWO-funded Open Competition Large project involving PI dr. Jenny Audring (Leiden University) and external partner prof. dr. Sjef Barbiers (Instituut voor de Nederlandse Taal).

Tasks and responsibilities
  • Extracting word-formation patterns from the existing descriptive literature and encoding them in systematic constructional schemas;
  • Matching complex words to the appropriate schemas and subschemas and annotating them in such a way that the inventory of constructions can be transformed into a network;
  • Assisting in finding, testing and evaluating digital tools, including LLMs, to aid classification, annotation and network building;
  • Investigating Dutch morphological constructions quantitatively and qualitatively;
  • Presenting (joint) research results at workshops and conferences;
  • Publishing (joint) research results and writing a PhD-thesis within the period of appointment;
  • (Assisting in) teaching activities at bachelor level;
  • Participating in (the organisation of) knowledge dissemination activities;
  • Participating in meetings and training sessions of the project research group.

Selection criteria
  • A Master’s degree in linguistics, completed before the start date;
  • Demonstrable interest in grammar, especially morphology, from a descriptive and/or theoretical perspective;
  • Native or near-native proficiency of Dutch and a good command of academic English;
  • Excellent research and analytical skills;
  • Experience in computational linguistics and/or affinity with the framework of Construction Grammar is a plus.

Terms and conditions
Appointment will be according to the terms of the Collective Labour Agreement of Dutch Universities (CAO Nederlandse Universiteiten). The employment will be for a period of four years. The first contract will be for 12 months with an extension for the following 36 months contingent on performance and compatibility. You are expected to work in Leiden and the appointment must lead to the completion of a PhD thesis.

Salary range from € 3.204.- gross per month in the first year for a fulltime appointment to € 4,051.- in the fourth year (pay scale for PhDs, in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities), plus substantial additional holiday and year-end allowances. Candidates from outside the Netherlands may be eligible for a substantial tax break.

Starting date: January 2027; a later starting date can be negotiated.

Research at our faculty/institute
Leiden University Centre for Linguistics (LUCL) is one of seven Institutes that falls under the Faculty of Humanities. With over 120 linguists working at the Institute, it is a rich research environment that prides itself on fostering scientific excellence. At LUCL we offer extensive research support to our researchers.

LUCL has a longstanding tradition in the study of the world’s languages and features unique linguistic expertise. Current theoretical insights are combined with modern experimental methods in its research profile area ‘Language Diversity in the World’. Researchers from our six umbrella research groups are experts in their respective fields while finding innovative ways of collaborating with colleagues in other fields and disciplines.

The Faculty of Humanities at Leiden University is a unique international centre for the advanced study of languages, cultures, arts, and societies worldwide, in their historical contexts from prehistory to the present. Our faculty is home to more than 6,000 students and 800 staff members. For more information see: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/humanities.

Diversity
Fostering an inclusive community is a central element of the values and vision of Leiden University. Leiden University is committed to becoming an inclusive community which enables all students and staff to feel valued and respected and to develop their full potential. Diversity in experiences and perspectives enriches our teaching and strengthens our research. High quality teaching and research is inclusive.

Questions?
For further information on the research project and the PhD position please contact the PI, dr. Jenny Audring, j.audring@hum.leidenuniv.nl

For practical questions, please contact the Institute Manager, Maarit van Gammeren: m.s.k.van.gammeren@hum.leidenuniv.nl.

Applications
Applications should be submitted no later than 1 November, 2026 via the blue button in our application system. Your application should include the following information:

  • A writing sample, preferably your MA thesis and an article or term paper that you wrote that pertains to the topic of the position;

jobs.title: Promovendus voor het project “Lerende Aanpak Vitaal Limburg”
jobs.description_html:
Achtergrond

Bij de Regio Deals werken Rijk en regio als partners samen om belangrijke opgaven in Nederland aan te pakken en de brede welvaart te vergroten. In Provincie Limburg zijn vier Regio Deals actief die gezamenlijk geografisch de hele provincie Limburg beslaan. Een unieke situatie die in de nabije toekomst ook zal doorwerken in het Nationaal Programma Vitale Regio’s (NPVR).

In de Limburgse Regio Deals staan het vergroten van de brede welvaart en het aanpakken van complexe maatschappelijke vraagstukken zoals talentontwikkeling en sociaal-economische achterstanden centraal. Om hierin meerwaarde te behalen, willen de provincie en regio’s structureel leren van de praktijk en systematisch inzicht krijgen in wat werkt, waarom het werkt, en waar ruimte is voor verbetering.

De uitgebreide achtergrond bij dit project is hier beschikbaar.

Het project

Het project is ingericht langs twee parallelle lijnen. De eerste lijn is de projectlijn: hiervoor worden in elke regio een of twee specifieke regiodeal-projecten geselecteerd waar mee wordt gewerkt. De tweede lijn is de structurele lijn: hiervoor wordt met geselecteerde gemeenten gewerkt, die dan zelf hun prioriteiten aangeven ter bepaling van de scope.

Lijn

Projectlijn: Betrekken van één of twee concrete Regio Deal-projecten per regio om samen te monitoren, leren en verbeteren.

Structurele lijn: Samenwerken met geselecteerde gemeenten aan structurele leerbehoeften en beleidsverbetering.

Drie pijlers vormen de kern van de methodologie en de werkwijze die binnen beide lijnen wordt gehanteerd. De eerste pijler is het gelaagde definitielandschap als instrument om beredeneerd tot te monitoren indicatoren te komen (zie voor de basis hiervan https://doi.org/mr4n). Hierbij worden verbindingen gelegd met reeds lopende initiatieven vanuit de Regio's met de monitoringspartij RIGO en het ministerie van BZK in het kader van het NPVR. De tweede pijler is het gebruik van de DOELWIT methode, een gegeneraliseerde, multidisciplinaire vorm van Acyclic Behavior Change Diagrams’ (ABCDs, zie https://doi.org/jp9t). Deze methode helpt om op een systematische manier te leren over tussenliggende doelen en werkingsmechanismen van maatregelen en interventies. De derde pijler is de structurele inbedding in organisaties. Voor beide lijnen worden Leerstructuren opgezet, waarin professionals samen komen en tussentijdse voortgang bespreken.

Pijler

1. Gelaagd definitielandschap: Gezamenlijk met stakeholders de doelen eenduidig definiëren en doel-indicatoren ontwikkelen op verschillende niveaus.

2. Systeemdenken met de DOELWIT methode: Systematisch leren begrijpen van werkingsmechanismen en tussenliggende doelen per interventie.

3. Structurele inbedding: Werkwijze verankeren via datagedreven monitoringssystemen en Leerstructuren in organisaties.

Werkwijze

Dit project is vormgegeven rondom nieuwe inzichten uit de sociale wetenschappen. Het is dus een uniek project, en dat betekent dat het mogelijk is dat we de werkzaamheden over tijd bijstellen. Op dit moment zijn de volgende werkzaamheden voorzien.

Je zult contact leggen met sleutelfiguren bij de provincie, de vier regio’s, en de geselecteerde gemeenten. Met hen zul je tijdens de vier jaar die het project loopt de Leerstructuren opzetten. Bovendien zul je samen met hen groepjes professionals begeleiden in het uitwerken van gelaagde definitielandschappen, het invullen van DOELWIT tabellen en het produceren van de bijbehorende DOELWIT diagrammen, en het selecteren of ontwikkelen van indicatoren. In dit proces werk je samen met hen ook aan structurele inbedding van die drie processen. Op deze manier implementeer je een structurende lerende werkwijze bij de provincie, de regio’s, en de geselecteerde gemeenten.

Je documenteert dit proces via veldnotities en opnames. Deze bronnen codeer je als kwalitatieve data met de Reproducible Open Coding Kit (https://doi.org/qcf6). Op deze manier leren we ook van dit proces. Door te kijken naar de diversiteit in gemeenten en tussen de gemeenten en de regio’s kunnen we toewerken naar een draaiboek om deze lerende aanpak ook bij andere overheidsinstanties te implementeren.

Je denkt na over methoden en conceptuele instrumenten (met conceptuele instrumenten bedoelen we dingen als de Decentralized Construct Taxonomy specifications uit https://doi.org/mr4n en de DOELWIT methode en ABCDs) die overheden en andere instanties kunnen ondersteunen bij de lerende aanpak. Die conceptuele instrumenten en methoden implementeren we in open software zodat ze ook makkelijk toegankelijk worden.

In dit project pas je de open science principes toe: we streven ernaar alle data openbaar te maken, net als alle materialen, analysescripts, en ontwikkelde software. We publiceren artikelen eerst als preprint en preregistreren geplande dataverzamelingen. We werken bij voorkeur alleen met open source software zoals R en andere open infrastructuur zoals OpenAlex en het Open Science Framework.

Je begeleidingsteam in dit uitdagende project bestaat uit A. Verbraak (Provincie Limburg), R. Crutzen (Universiteit Maastricht), G-J. Peters (OU), en dagelijks begeleiders C. van Vliet en T. Gültzow (ook beiden OU). Daarnaast heeft het project een adviescommissie die bestaat uit sleutelfiguren uit verschillende domeinen en van verschillende niveaus, van burgers tot en met het rijk, zodat die pluriforme perspectieven het projectteam en de Leerstructuren kunnen voeden. Je wordt onderdeel van de vakgroep Theory, Methoden, en Statistiek van de Faculteit Psychologie van de OU, en zoals we het nu voor ons zien werk je drie dagen bij de Provincie, een dag bij de UM, en een dag bij de OU. Tot slot zul je waarschijnlijk veel samenwerken met collega’s van VERLICHT, het monitoringsproject van Heerlen-Noord, dat ook bij de OU is ondergebracht (https://verlicht.one).

jobs.title: PhD Position on Linguistic Effects of Child Language Brokering in Multilingual Families
jobs.description_html:
We are recruiting two PhD candidates for an interdisciplinary project on child language brokering - how multilingual children translate and mediate for others in everyday life. You will investigate how these experiences shape linguistic (this position) or socio-emotional development (the other position) in children and their parents. Are you interested in multilingualism, diverse research methods, and team science? Apply now!

About the position
Children from immigrant families often translate and mediate for others (typically their parents), a phenomenon called “child language brokering”. Brokering occurs in a variety of contexts: at home, at schools, and in medical offices. Research shows that child language brokering may have positive and negative effects on children’s socio-emotional development and on child-parent relationships, depending on when and where brokering occurs. There are also some indications that brokering affects children’s and parents’ development of the first and second language, but these effects remain largely unexplored.

In this PhD project, you will investigate how brokering experiences affect the maintenance of the heritage language and development of the second language in child brokers and their parents. The project is part of an NWO-funded project, consisting of two PhD students and a team of supervisors. The other PhD project focuses on the socio-emotional effects of brokering.

You will conduct a series of studies to investigate the effects of child brokering on the maintenance of the heritage language and development of the second language across more informal (home) and more formal (school, health care) contexts. You will also investigate what linguistic strategies are used during brokering, what beliefs brokers and parents hold about these strategies, and what opportunities for language learning emerge during brokering episodes. You will use a variety of methods, including observations, semi-structured interviews, controlled language tasks, as well as advanced statistics (network analysis). Together, the studies you will conduct will inform us about when and how brokering has positive effects on the use, maintenance and development of the heritage language and the second language in both child brokers and their parents.

This is what you will be doing
You will perform the following tasks and activities:
  • reviewing literature on the effects of language brokering on the heritage and second language;
  • carrying out in-depth studies to investigate the effects of child brokering on language development, as well as the linguistic strategies used during brokering and the opportunities to learn language during brokering;
  • collaborating in an interdisciplinary research team;
  • committing to open science practices such as pre-registering studies;
  • contributing to knowledge utilization (outreach) activities undertaken by the team;
  • submission of a PhD thesis within the period of appointment;
  • presenting intermediate research results at workshops and conferences;
  • participating in the Research School and Faculty of Humanities PhD training programmes;
  • co-teaching courses at BA-level in the second and third year of the appointment (maximum 0,2 fte per year).

This is what we ask of you
  • a completed Master's degree in Linguistics, Education, Psychology or a related field;
